item.title: Jose Mourinho produces vintage knee slide after beating Barcelona in El Clasico
item.description: Jose Mourinho produced a vintage knee slide as Real Madrid dramatically defeated rivals Barcelona 2-1 in El Classico at Camp Nou. The 63-year-old manager was taking charge of the fixture for the first time since his return to the Real Madrid dugout, 13 years after the end of his first spell at the club . Kylian Mbappé with what could be a late winner for Real Madrid! 😱😱 Wild celebrations from Los Blancos, including a Jose Mourinho knee slide, as an away Clásico win beckons! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/c05FU3kdp1 — Premier Sports (@PremSportsTV) October 25, 2026 And his players produced a statement performance to hand LaLiga leaders Barcelona their first defeat of the season, as Kylian Mbappe scored a brace. Mbappe’s winner, in the 88th minute, saw Mourinho drop to his knees and punch the air – recreating one of the most iconic moments of his managerial career. The Portuguese famously celebrated Inter Milan’s Champions League semi-final victory over Barcelona in 2010 by running onto the Camp Nou pitch and doing a knee slide on the turf. “It was the most difficult match, against the highest quality opponent, one that had only won in the league," Mourinho said afterwards. “For us, it's the victory with the most impressive performance.” Mourinho’s celebration at Camp Nou in the 2010 Champions League semi-finals (Getty) Both sides created a series of half-chances early on, but Real's forays forward came with far more resolve. Barca manager ​Hansi ⁠Flick's frustration on the touchline served as evidence that Mourinho's game plan was functioning better than his own. In the 41st minute Yan Diomande crossed from the left and Gerard Martin's soft clearance hit the onrushing Mbappe, bouncing off him and into the net. Barcelona had the chance to level before the break after a fortunate ricochet, but Lamine Yamal couldn't convert from close range. It was a set piece that undid Real in the 61st minute, with Pedri's reverse pass finding Raphinha in space in the box and the Brazilian finishing into the corner. Real's swift movement of the ball in their own half continued ⁠to expose the Barcelona backline in the early stages of the second half. However, following the goal, the visitors found it increasingly hard to escape Barcelona's pressing. Barcelona's attacks were now finishing with last-ditch blocks from the Real defence, even if Mourinho's side continued to carry a threat going forward. That defensive conviction was rewarded with three minutes remaining. A loose touch from Barcelona ‌substitute Gabriel Jesus set Real on the counter-attack, and substitute ​Eduardo Camavinga had enough pace to get in behind the defence, ‌before squaring the ball for ⁠Mbappe to tap into the empty net. Includes reporting from Reuters

item.title: Lakers’ Walker Kessler gets 100% real on cooling off against Jazz
item.description: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Lakers’ Walker Kessler gets 100% real on cooling off against Jazz appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler was showered with boos on his return to Delta Center on Sunday. But in the end, he had the last laugh as the Lakers beat the Jazz, 132-123, to stay undefeated at 3-0. Luka Doncic went off for 52 points on 17-of-30 field goals, including 8-of-13 from beyond the arc. He added eight rebounds, 10 assists, and two steals. After a hot start in his first season with the Lakers, Kessler was limited to two points on two attempts. He had seven rebounds. In a report from the Los Angeles Times’ Thuc Ngi Nguyen, the 25-year-old center admitted that he may have been too excited to face his former team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I let my emotions get the best of me,” said Kessler. “Kind of got too amped and then just couldn’t find the ball. Couldn’t find the rhythm, just kind of was off a couple fouls that were tough, a couple blocks I usually (make). It’s one of those nights. But fortunately, basketball is not a one-man sport.” Entering the game against the Jazz, Kessler was averaging 24 points on 85.7% shooting, 8.5 rebounds, 1.5 steals, and 4.0 blocks. He bolted Utah in the offseason and signed with Los Angeles for four years worth $130 million. He played four years with the Jazz, who drafted him with the No. 22 pick in 2022. The former SEC Defensive Player of the Year will continue to play a major role for the Lakers, who have been crying for a dependable pivot since trading Anthony Davis to the Dallas Mavericks for Doncic. Kessler will try to bounce back on Tuesday against the Portland Trail Blazers. Related: What Lakers’ Luka Doncic told Walker Kessler after big man’s struggles vs. Jazz Related: Luka Doncic’s response to Kendrick Perkins after 52-point eruption goes viral

item.title: Real Madrid attacking duo share hilarious exchange after El Clasico victory over Barcelona: ‘He is my wolf’
item.description: Real Madrid attacking duo share hilarious exchange after El Clasico victory over Barcelona: ‘He is my wolf’ Real Madrid played a near-perfect game to secure a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou . It was followed by a light-hearted moment involving Kylian Mbappe and Yan Diomande, offering a glimpse of the growing chemistry between the two attackers. In an interaction after the match, the French superstar and the young winger exchanged playful remarks that quickly drew attention. Mbappe and Diomande share a funny moment The moment suggested that the duo are developing a strong relationship away from the pitch. “He is my wolf,” Mbappe said while referring to Diomande. The youngster responded with an equally amusing comment: “He is my little brother.” The exchange was brief, but it captured the relaxed atmosphere surrounding Madrid’s players after securing an important victory against their biggest rivals. Both attackers have become important figures in Jose Mourinho’s plans, bringing different qualities to the team’s forward line. Mbappe provides experience, movement and a proven goalscoring threat, as evidenced by his brace against Barcelona. Diomande, on the other hand, hugs the left touchline and offers direct running, dribbling, pace and the ability to cause chaos. The duo seem to be developing an excellent understanding on the pitch in the absence of Vinicius Junior. A promising partnership for Mourinho Beyond the humour, the interaction offers an encouraging sign of the relationship between a player who has been at the club for a while and a newcomer. For younger footballers, settling into a demanding dressing room can be challenging, particularly at a club where expectations are consistently high. Real Madrid played an excellent game against Barcelona on Sunday night. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Having an established superstar like Mbappe put his arm around a teammate’s shoulder can help create a positive environment. It is still early days, but the two Los Blancos attackers seem to be getting along quite nicely, both on and off the pitch. In the victory over Barcelona, the entire team played for one another and looked determined to secure the three points. This is the kind of spirit that Jose Mourinho keeps insisting on, and going forward, he will want to see more of this. Ultimately, Madrid handled the occasion of the Clasico to perfection and will hope to do so in many more games going forward.

item.title: Barcelona to send three first-team stars to London for Ballon d’Or ceremony as Cubarsi’s absence raises questions
item.description: Barcelona to send three first-team stars to London for Ballon d’Or ceremony as Cubarsi’s absence raises questions Barcelona are preparing to travel to London for the Ballon d’Or gala, with Lamine Yamal, Rodri Hernandez and Joan Garcia among the first-team players included on the club’s planned delegation. As per SPORT , the group is scheduled to depart from the corporate terminal at El Prat airport at 12:15 p.m. on Monday, ahead of the ceremony at The London Palladium. The event marks the 70th edition of the prestigious awards and will be held outside Paris for the first time. Barcelona will have several reasons to follow the ceremony closely, with Yamal competing for two individual honours and Garcia in contention for the award recognising the world’s best goalkeeper. Lamine Yamal targets another Kopa Trophy and Ballon d’Or success Yamal is among the leading names to watch at the ceremony, having been nominated for both the Ballon d’Or and the Kopa Trophy, which recognises the best young player in men’s football. The Barcelona winger could win the Kopa Trophy for the third consecutive year after claiming the award in 2024 and 2025. Lamine Yamal is a favourite to win the Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images) His Ballon d’Or nomination also places him among the leading contenders for the sport’s most prestigious individual prize. Rodri and Joan Garcia nominated for major individual awards Rodri will also represent Barcelona at the ceremony, having been included among the 30 Ballon d’Or contenders. The midfielder won the award in 2024 while playing for Manchester City and is back among the nominees following his move to Barcelona. Joan Garcia, meanwhile, is in contention for the Yashin Trophy, which recognises the best goalkeeper in men’s football. The shot-stopper earned his nomination after winning the Zamora Trophy in his first season as a Barcelona player, giving him an opportunity to receive recognition on the international stage. Cubarsi will not travel with the Barcelona delegates. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images) The three players offer Barcelona representation across the main individual awards, the young-player category and the goalkeeper prize. Pau Cubarsí’s absence leaves a question One notable omission from the planned travel list is Pau Cubarsi, who has been nominated for both the Ballon d’Or and the Kopa Trophy. His absence could change if the club updates its arrangements before departure, but no last-minute inclusion has been confirmed in the information available. Barcelona’s delegation will therefore be worth monitoring as the ceremony approaches. With Yamal chasing another Kopa Trophy, Rodri seeking further Ballon d’Or recognition and Garcia competing for the Yashin Trophy, the London event could prove an important night for the club’s individual award hopefuls.

item.title: Enes Kanter reveals why parents should never let their daughters date NBA players
item.description: Photo by Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Enes Kanter Freedom has made a striking claim about the NBA’s off-court culture, warning parents against letting their daughters date professional athletes after alleging that more than 95 per cent of NBA players cheat. The former Utah Jazz centre shared his views during an appearance on Savannah Chrisley’s podcast Unlocked , recalling an unusual rookie responsibility that gave him an insight into the private lives of his teammates. Kanter entered the NBA as the third overall pick in the 2011 Draft after playing professionally in Turkey as a teenager. His time with the Jazz apparently exposed him to behaviour that has stayed with him throughout his career. Enes Kanter explains his warning about NBA players Kanter revealed that one of his rookie duties was to look after his teammates’ second phones whenever the Jazz travelled to Utah. He explained: “One of my rookie duties was whenever we travel to Utah, because I was playing in Utah, they all give me their second phones. I had to charge all 12 phones and whenever we go back on the road, I had to bring (them all).” Kanter said he carried the phones in a large bag before handing them back to the players when the team travelled again. He also claimed to have witnessed women waiting for NBA players in hotel rooms, prompting his blunt advice to parents. “To all the parents out there… If I have a daughter, I would not let her date an athlete, especially an NBA player,” Kanter said. “I know some of the stories and we could get to it if you want, but I think over 95 percent — and I’m being nice — of the NBA players cheat.” The figure is Kanter’s personal claim and has not been independently established by the material provided. His comments follow previous allegations about the league’s off-court culture. During his time with the Boston Celtics in the 2019-20 season, Kanter also described teammates sharing access to a premium OnlyFans account. He said he declined to participate, explaining that he did not want to watch the content and believed he had “better morals”. Kanter has never been shy about expressing controversial opinions, and his latest remarks offer another glimpse into his experiences during his NBA career. item.title: Mum wants grassroots football to be more inclusive
item.description: "We were told that if [Arthur] didn't improve, he would be removed from the team," says mum Millie [BBC] A parent and GP is pushing for grassroots football to be more inclusive after her son, who has dyspraxia, felt forced out of his club for being a "weaker player". Millie has said her eight-year-old son Arthur's condition affects his balance, co-ordination and processing, and he was given less game time than his peers until he stopped playing. She said she would like all children to be able to "go and play at their local team, play alongside their friends, and for it to be genuinely inclusive". Derbyshire County Football Association's (DCFA) Luke Wilkinson said Arthur's story had "raised awareness of the gaps in provision" and invited Millie to join the body's neurodiversity working group. Football development officer Luke Wilkinson invited more parents to talk to the Derbyshire County FA about their children's experience of grassroots football [BBC] Wilkinson took on the role of football development officer at DCFA four months ago, working across female football, disability and inclusion. He said listening to Arthur's story was "a big learning curve" and was keen to bring Millie's "passion and GP expertise" on to their neurodiversity working group. "If you're going through that same experience, don't hide it. Come and talk to us and let's see how can we help you and your child, or children, keep playing the sport," he said. Wilkinson explained that the association offered a range of disability specific provision, including Comets, a pan-disability football programme for five to 11 year olds. However, he said bringing those Comets players into mainstream grassroots football was an area for the FA to work on, but felt confident this could be achieved as part of 2040 FA strategy. He also said he was looking to develop a bespoke Derbyshire neurodiversity module for mainstream coaches to "learn and make their club more inclusive". Eight-year-old Arthur said children like him were less included at football clubs because of their disabilities [BBC] Arthur started playing football from age four and was excited to sign up to his first Under 7s side. "I love having a kick about with my friends, keeping myself moving, I enjoy the sport and I like socialising with my team," Arthur said. But after being part of the club for a year and a half, Arthur found he was getting "significantly less" playing time than the other children. "I was getting subbed loads and loads of times. I was only coming on to the pitch for like 15 or 20 minutes and I just started to feel less valued," he said. "He lost his confidence, he'd lost the love of the game, he started to say he didn't really want to go and he wasn't enjoying it," said his mum, Millie. She raised the issue with the coaches but was told her son was a "weaker player" and the team needed to "focus on winning". Derbyshire County Football Association's (DCFA) Luke Wilkinson said Arthur's story had "raised awareness of the gaps in provision" and invited Millie to join the body's neurodiversity working group. Football development officer Luke Wilkinson invited more parents to talk to the Derbyshire County FA about their children's experience of grassroots football [BBC] Wilkinson took on the role of football development officer at DCFA four months ago, working across female football, disability and inclusion. He said listening to Arthur's story was "a big learning curve" and was keen to bring Millie's "passion and GP expertise" on to their neurodiversity working group. "If you're going through that same experience, don't hide it. Come and talk to us and let's see how can we help you and your child, or children, keep playing the sport," he said. Wilkinson explained that the association offered a range of disability specific provision, including Comets, a pan-disability football programme for five to 11 year olds. However, he said bringing those Comets players into mainstream grassroots football was an area for the FA to work on, but felt confident this could be achieved as part of 2040 FA strategy. He also said he was looking to develop a bespoke Derbyshire neurodiversity module for mainstream coaches to "learn and make their club more inclusive". Eight-year-old Arthur said children like him were less included at football clubs because of their disabilities [BBC] Arthur started playing football from age four and was excited to sign up to his first Under 7s side. "I love having a kick about with my friends, keeping myself moving, I enjoy the sport and I like socialising with my team," Arthur said. But after being part of the club for a year and a half, Arthur found he was getting "significantly less" playing time than the other children. "I was getting subbed loads and loads of times. I was only coming on to the pitch for like 15 or 20 minutes and I just started to feel less valued," he said. "He lost his confidence, he'd lost the love of the game, he started to say he didn't really want to go and he wasn't enjoying it," said his mum, Millie. She raised the issue with the coaches but was told her son was a "weaker player" and the team needed to "focus on winning". "We were told that if he didn't improve, he would be removed from the team," said Millie, who requested not to name the team, because she was confident this was a wider issue across grassroots clubs, having spoken with other affected families. Arthur said he felt "less valued" by his coaches and eventually left his grassroots club [BBC] One of those was a football coach and dad of three, who said his middle child had been given less playing time than his peers. "It's honestly unfair. They come home upset. Boys being boys, they taunt each other and take the mickey, that makes them more upset and parents have to deal with it," said the dad, who asked to remain anonymous. He said he kept a record of the playing time of each his players and gives each child equal playing time and opportunities to play in all positions. "For us as coaches, we don't always need to take it so seriously and remember why we're doing it - to allow them to play football, for the fun of it, and that's something the children can take into later life," he added. Millie has looked at other football opportunities for Arthur but said trials for "mid to high level players" were stopping her son from accessing the sport. Arthur said: "I've been to a lot of clubs and autistic, ADHD, dyspraxia children, like myself, aren't getting included as much because of their disabilities. People take it the wrong way and say they can't be in the club." His mum added: "If their lasting experience, as a child aged eight, is being told they weren't good enough, they might be put off football for life." Vicci Wells OBE is the assistant director of children and young people for the charity Youth Sport Trust. Having heard Arthur's story, she said "children develop at different rates and in different ways". "To help them succeed means we need coaches who are curious about what helps that individual child, rather than expecting every child to learn and perform in exactly the same way," she added. "Inclusion is about much more than giving a child the opportunity to join a team. "It is about creating an environment where they feel they belong, valued and able to participate in a way that meaningfully works for them." Sophia Prout, business manager at Neurodiverse Sport, has investigated neuroinclusion in community sport. She said there was "little to no resources available focusing on neurodiversity". "Neurodivergence was more visible than ever, yet coaches and community leaders were largely learning on the job," she said. The organisation has worked together with the charity, StreetGames, to provide a free online course to help coaches, or those working at community sports organisations, learn more about the needs of neurodivergent athletes and participants. Listen to BBC Radio Derby on Sounds and follow BBC Derby on Facebook , on X , or on Instagram . Send your story ideas to eastmidsnews@bbc.co.uk or via WhatsApp on 0808 100 2210. item.title: Who slept best last night: Liam Lawson
item.description: Motorsport photo Jolyon Palmer wasn't trying to be creative when he asked Liam Lawson about his future during F1 TV's live post-race coverage. It was simply a question anyone would ask – perhaps even Lawson himself. The sort of question you ask without really expecting an answer, more out of wonderment as to why the answer isn't already an obvious yes. "Another race, another win, in the race that you were in, really, the midfield battle," the former Renault driver and now one of F1's top analysts put to Lawson after a couple of questions from his colleagues. And then added: "When are you going to be announced for next year?" There shouldn't really be any questions about whether Lawson deserves to stay in F1, and with his current team. Any team on its way to securing the best result in its F1 history would surely have already tied down the driver responsible for the biggest share of its points. Any such team wouldn't want him to become impatient or feel insecure. No one would be talking about Liam Lawson's future had he been racing for almost any other team and the only reason for a potential delay would probably be his management demanding better terms for their client. Were Lawson delivering these performances for another outfit, he'd probably be asking for more money, less social media time and no more easyJet flights. But that's not the case. Because he is indeed racing for Racing Bulls . And he is a Red Bull driver. And nothing is ever straightforward when you are. Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls "I've no idea, man," Lawson laughed in response. "Honestly, at the moment, it's to a point where I'm not even really thinking about it. I'm just pressing on and enjoying the races, honestly." And there's no reason to think Lawson is actually stressing about his unsettled future. He's been in this position long enough to stop wondering about the same questions outside observers are constantly asking about Red Bull's driver decisions. Those on the outside, back in the winter of 2024, could have asked: why on earth does a guy with just 11 F1 starts get promoted? Or, a few months later: how the hell do you give the guy just two races – and then sack him? Or now: what else does this guy need to do to secure his seat for next season? It was simply a question anyone would ask – perhaps even Lawson himself. The sort of question you ask without really expecting an answer, more out of wonderment as to why the answer isn't already an obvious yes. "Another race, another win, in the race that you were in, really, the midfield battle," the former Renault driver and now one of F1's top analysts put to Lawson after a couple of questions from his colleagues. And then added: "When are you going to be announced for next year?" There shouldn't really be any questions about whether Lawson deserves to stay in F1, and with his current team. Any team on its way to securing the best result in its F1 history would surely have already tied down the driver responsible for the biggest share of its points. Any such team wouldn't want him to become impatient or feel insecure. No one would be talking about Liam Lawson's future had he been racing for almost any other team and the only reason for a potential delay would probably be his management demanding better terms for their client. Were Lawson delivering these performances for another outfit, he'd probably be asking for more money, less social media time and no more easyJet flights. But that's not the case. Because he is indeed racing for Racing Bulls . And he is a Red Bull driver. And nothing is ever straightforward when you are. Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls "I've no idea, man," Lawson laughed in response. "Honestly, at the moment, it's to a point where I'm not even really thinking about it. I'm just pressing on and enjoying the races, honestly." And there's no reason to think Lawson is actually stressing about his unsettled future. He's been in this position long enough to stop wondering about the same questions outside observers are constantly asking about Red Bull's driver decisions. Those on the outside, back in the winter of 2024, could have asked: why on earth does a guy with just 11 F1 starts get promoted? Or, a few months later: how the hell do you give the guy just two races – and then sack him? Or now: what else does this guy need to do to secure his seat for next season? But for Lawson, it's probably just the norm. There's no reason to stress about it – whatever happens, happens. So he's just pressing on and enjoying the races, really. And it's going bloody well. There's not much to tell about his race in Austin. Just like Kimi Antonelli's - what do you actually explain about the Italian's victory in Texas? There's really not a lot: perfectly executed, brilliantly delivered, controlled. You can think of another couple of adjectives – but there won't be much substance to attach them to. There wasn't much drama. He seemingly cruised to victory. And Lawson did pretty much the same in the midfield. Read Also: Winners and losers from F1's United States Grand Prix He had a good qualifying session, reaching Q3 once again, and accepted the team's request not to go out in the final segment to help his team-mate, who had a grid penalty. But he was still ninth on the grid – effectively a midfield pole in modern F1. Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Pierre Gasly, Alpine, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls, Pierre Gasly, Alpine, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team A very clean start followed. He kept Pierre Gasly behind going up the hill into Turn 1, then slotted in right behind the McLarens. He built a gap, made his pitstop and delivered a perfectly managed stint to the finish on hard tyres. No drama. No stress. Just execution. "For us, it's been a very strong race, and a strong weekend," he told the media after the finish. "Executed well, so very very happy. And obviously going to the next few races, some interesting tracks. But the car has been working well, so it should hopefully work well there too." He'd had a lot more stress on Thursday, performing his first proper live concert with his friends in Austin. "I mean, today was like 10% of that," he joked in his conversation with Palmer and his colleagues. Ninth was the best he could have achieved, with no retirements among F1's leading four teams. That's another midfield win for Lawson, who also comfortably leads the unofficial midfield championship this year. Yes, sure, he had a couple of races with Red Bull, but who's to say he'd have scored significantly fewer points had he raced for Racing Bulls instead? Maybe a couple. Anyway, his 'championship lead' over Pierre Gasly is now 35 points – which is huge – and he looks likely to remain ninth in the standings until the end of the year. There's no official title for being 'best of the rest', but it's usually a description of a very strong season. Back in the day, when the Faenza team was still called Toro Rosso and run by a calm and quiet Austrian named Franz Tost, its goal almost every single year was to finish fifth in the constructors' championship. Tost declared it as a target almost routinely in his media appearances ahead of each new season – but the team never quite got there under his leadership. This year could finally be the year! Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls The former Toro Rosso squad is now the only midfield team with more than 100 points, and Alpine doesn't look particularly close anymore. Especially when you consider just how quick and handy these Racing Bulls cars have become; and it's Lawson who's making most of the difference for Tost's former team. So... why is he still not signed for next year? It could be that it's just a formality, and Racing Bulls simply needs to finalise its 2027 plans for Nikola Tsolov before announcing Lawson's extension. But with Red Bull, you just never know. Part of the team's identity is to find the next Sebastian Vettel or Max Verstappen , and that sometimes means promoting juniors at the expense of established drivers. It's happened many times in the past, and it will probably happen again. But if Lawson is shown the door after the year he's had, it would be one of the cruellest decisions in Red Bull's history of handling drivers. There's absolutely no reason to rush Tsolov either. Yes, he's one of the main title contenders in F2, but it's not as though Red Bull desperately needs another superstar junior right now. With Max Verstappen's contract extended and Isack Hadjar doing exactly what he should be doing, there's no need to add more pressure to the system. There's Arvid Lindblad , after all, whose potential still needs to be confirmed in his second year – and there's no better measuring stick than Lawson in his current form. There's only one logical decision, really. But with Red Bull, you just never know, right? Read Also: Max Verstappen pinpoints two recurring Red Bull problems: "We should use sign language!" item.title: Sinfield 'should have been Sir Kevin years ago', Prince William says
item.description: The Prince of Wales has praised former rugby league captain Sir Kevin Sinfield , saying he should have received his knighthood “years ago”. The rugby coach and motor neurone disease (MND) campaigner was one of 60 people to receive honours from William at a recent investiture ceremony at Windsor Castle . Sir Kevin, who has raised millions for charity, received a knighthood for his services to the MND community, as well as for services to league and union rugby. Speaking to BBC Breakfast , the prince said: “I think, frankly, he should have been Sir Kevin years ago. “I don’t know how he keeps going, I’m worried about his knees, I’m worried about his hips. The guy is just a machine. “He’s a top bloke, really nice guy, good, honest, kind, decent northerner and I love that about Kevin, that there is no ego with him. He is what you get.” The Prince and Princess of Wales recently surprised Sir Kevin in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, as he completed the third day of his final 7 in 7 running challenges. William (left) met Rob Burrow (right) and Kevin Sinfield during a visit to Headingley Stadium in Leeds in 2024 (Phil Noble/PA) The challenge involved completing an ultra-marathon every day for seven days. The fundraiser was inspired by his former Leeds Rhinos teammate Rob Burrow , who died in 2024 after living with MND for four-and-a-half years. The prince said he had also written a letter to Mr Burrow’s family. “Everyone grieves differently and every circumstance is different, so you need to take your time over it,” he said. “It’s always better to say something around grief than it is to ignore it.” Former rugby player and charity fundraiser Kevin Sinfield poses with their medal after being appointed as a Knight Bachelor (AFP/Getty) Speaking about receiving his knighthood, Sir Kevin previously said he was “massively humbled by the whole experience” and “very proud to accept it on behalf of the MND community and their families”. The 46-year-old said William, who presented Sir Kevin and Mr Burrow with CBEs at Headingley Stadium in 2024, had been “fantastically supportive” of their campaign. Sir Kevin told the Press Association: “I think he champions pulling communities together and I have seen how the MND community have come together on the back of Rob’s diagnosis and several other high-profile sportspeople over the last six or seven years. “So, his support and, obviously, Princess Catherine’s as well, they’ve been wonderful and bring a real credibility to what we’re trying to do.”

item.title: Torquay's 'Prince of Plainmoor' Stubbs dies aged 85
item.description: Robin Stubbs is regarded as one of Torquay United's greatest-ever players [Shutterstock] Robin Stubbs - widely regarded as one of Torquay United's greatest-ever players - has died aged 85. Dubbed 'The Prince of Plainmoor', Stubbs scored 133 goals in 263 games in two separate spells for the Gulls. He first moved to Plainmoor from Birmingham City in 1963 in a £6,000 deal and scored 24 goals in his first season in the old Division Four. Stubbs scored 39 goals a season later - two of which came in arguably his greatest game as he scored twice late on as Torquay secured a 3-3 draw with top flight Tottenham Hotspur in the FA Cup third round in front of more than 20,000 fans at Plainmoor. He equalised in the replay before the Gulls went on to lose 5-1 at White Hart Lane, although his goals helped Torquay win promotion the following season. Stubbs' goals earned Torquay an FA Cup replay with Tottenham Hotspur in 1965 [Shutterstock] Stubbs moved to Bristol Rovers in 1969, but after three seasons returned to Torquay where he finished his career in 1972. "Robin Stubbs was one of the greatest players ever to wear the yellow shirt," Torquay United co-chairman Michael Westcott told the club website. "His goals, his pace and the excitement he brought to Plainmoor made him a hero to generations of Torquay United supporters. "The title 'Prince of Plainmoor' was thoroughly deserved, but his place in the club's history rests on much more than the goals he scored. He gave people memories they carried with them for the rest of their lives. "Robin's connection with the club remained strong long after he stopped playing, and it was always a pleasure to welcome him and his family back to Plainmoor." Related internet links Torquay United

item.title: Man United told they face a major problem if they sack Michael Carrick
item.description: Man United told they face a major problem if they sack Michael Carrick Manchester United manager Michael Carrick’s time at Old Trafford appears to be numbered following the disappointing 3-0 defeat at the hands of Bournemouth on Sunday. The result leaves the Red Devils in 16th place in the league table after eight games, just a point above the relegation zone. The English giants have struggled to get going this season after a blockbuster end to the last campaign. United opted for a managerial change in January, with Carrick coming in to replace Ruben Amorim and guiding the club to a third-placed finish. Unfortunately, the English manager has failed to replicate that form this season, with his team losing six and winning just two of their 12 games in all competitions. For the record, the Premier League giants lost just two of their 17 games under Carrick last campaign. United are now winless in the last eight games across competitions, with five defeats and three draws. The situation has prompted the club hierarchy to consider another managerial upheaval. United eyeing several managers Recent reports suggest that United have already decided to part ways with Carrick, with Eddie Howe emerging as the frontrunner for the job. The former Newcastle United manager is available to take charge immediately, having ended his time with the Magpies this summer. Meanwhile, ex-Bayern Munich manager Julian Nagelsmann has also been named as an option . The German is also looking for his next assignment at the moment after leaving his post as the Die Mannschaft coach following a disappointing 2026 FIFA World Cup. Antonio Conte, who is also available after leaving Napoli this summer, was also touted as an option. However, the Italian has since distanced himself from those rumours. Other candidates include Brighton & Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler, who has also shut down any talk of an exit from the Amex. Former England goalkeeper Paul Robinson has now explained why managers will be wary of the Old Trafford job. United will struggle to find Carrick’s replacement In conversation on BBC Radio 5 Live after the game, Robinson was asked whether Carrick would be in charge for the upcoming match against Chelsea. He responded: “I can’t answer that honestly, I really don’t know because of how the club is. I think there’s so many different options.” “The club could decide to go in a different direction, and Michael Carrick, who would blame him if he turned around and went in a different direction?” The former Tottenham Hotspur custodian suggested that Carrick could lose his job, but warned that finding a replacement would not be easy. He continued: “To give you my opinion, I don’t think he will be, but for whichever reason, I don’t know. But then, from Manchester United’s perspective, who do you get? What do you want?” “Because Unai Emery’s not coming, and who wants to be in control of this football club? No one would touch them at the moment, and the way the club is and

item.title: Liverpool's long-term Alisson succession plan revealed
item.description: Liverpool's long-term Alisson succession plan revealed Liverpool's succession plan for Alisson Becker has been a topic of discussion for several years at Anfield. Many believed that Caoimhin Kelleher was the long-term heir to Alisson's number one spot, but the Irish 'keeper is now a number one in his own right at Brentford. Giorgi Mamardashvili appeared to be next in line when he first joined the Reds from Valencia, but the Georgian's development hasn't been as smooth as many would have hoped. Although Liverpool have a few other options coming through the academy, and Lucca Brughmans is due to arrive from Genk in July, it is becoming more accepted that the club will have to turn to the transfer market to replace Alisson. Liverpool monitoring Premier League 'keeper as Alisson heir With less than 12 months remaining on his contract, Alisson 's time at Anfield feels like it is coming to a close. The Reds may well look to extend the Brazilian's stay, but either way the 34-year-old is beginning to enter the twilight of his career. One of the more surprising names linked with a Merseyside move is Konstantinos Tzolakis, who joined newly promoted Premier League side Hull City in the summer. That's according to a report from Ekrem Konur , who claims Liverpool have been closely monitoring Tzolakis' development. The update states that Tzolakis' representatives have been informed that he would be among the Reds' top targets should the club enter the market for a goalkeeper next summer. The Greek international has kept three clean sheets in seven Premier League matches and also saved the only penalty he has faced so far in the division. Tzolakis joined Hull for a club record £20 million in the summer, and it would likely take a considerably larger fee to pry the 'keeper away after just one season assuming the Tigers stay up.

item.title: José Mourinho throws a bucket of cold water realism on Barcelona at Camp Nou
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - OCTOBER 25: Jose Mourinho, Head Coach of Real Madrid and Hansi Flick, Manager of FC Barcelona, embrace before the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid at Spotify Camp Nou on October 25, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a feeling of unease coming into this Clasico with José Mourinho making his return to the Camp Nou . In the end, this version of Real Madrid under the special one was actually exactly who we thought they were going to be, and yet, Barcelona struggled to react and find solutions. Before going into a righteous rant, it’s important to remind ourselves that the sky isn’t falling. The best path forward is to be calm and carry on. I’d much rather be Barcelona under Hansi Flick than Real Madrid under Mourinho. It really is the difference between all that is good and bad in football. Both teams are supremely talented, but Barcelona is the one who plays like protagonists. They were the ones who wanted the ball in order to create with it, while Real Madrid, as cynical as you would expect them to be under Mourinho, in spite of a roster full of world class players, sat back and waited for the Blaugrana to make mistakes. That was the whole ballgame, and it worked. Real Madrid implemented Mourinho’s tactics with aplomb. Eventually, Gerard Martín and Pau Cubarsí faltered in front of goal, and Kylian Mbappe was there to make them pay. Game over. Barcelona had all of the meaningful possession, but it didn’t matter because Real Madrid was happy to give it to them. What mattered was not allowing them space to be dangerous in. For the second big game in a row, Lamine Yamal, Barcelona’s superstar, put in a net negative performance. With the Ballon d’Or to be announced on Monday, he’ll head to the ceremony on the back of two defeats with Barca. Hansi Flick took a big gamble this week, prioritizing the Clasico over the Champions League. I don’t blame him for making that choice, and frankly I’m frustrated on his behalf that he was so short-handed defensively for such a choice to even have to be made. We can all have our opinions about what went wrong, but for me I can’t get over the fact that Barcelona, in October, are already running out of defenders. In Flick’s system nonetheless, and with the knowledge brought to light over the past two seasons that this was the team’s greatest vulnerability, how in the hell did we end the summer with two less defenders on the roster? I don’t even want to blame Cubarsí and Martín for their mistakes. Cubarsí is already being overloaded with minutes for Barcelona and Spain, while Martín has been playing this week while battling a niggling injury. For all the good João Cancelo can do, he was not brought in, I hope at least, to be Barelona’s starting full-back in games like these where his attacking strengths would be overshadowed by his weaknesses defensively. There were no good options for Flick this week. In part, is

With the Ballon d’Or to be announced on Monday, he’ll head to the ceremony on the back of two defeats with Barca. Hansi Flick took a big gamble this week, prioritizing the Clasico over the Champions League. I don’t blame him for making that choice, and frankly I’m frustrated on his behalf that he was so short-handed defensively for such a choice to even have to be made. We can all have our opinions about what went wrong, but for me I can’t get over the fact that Barcelona, in October, are already running out of defenders. In Flick’s system nonetheless, and with the knowledge brought to light over the past two seasons that this was the team’s greatest vulnerability, how in the hell did we end the summer with two less defenders on the roster? I don’t even want to blame Cubarsí and Martín for their mistakes. Cubarsí is already being overloaded with minutes for Barcelona and Spain, while Martín has been playing this week while battling a niggling injury. For all the good João Cancelo can do, he was not brought in, I hope at least, to be Barelona’s starting full-back in games like these where his attacking strengths would be overshadowed by his weaknesses defensively. There were no good options for Flick this week. In part, is this his fault for not demanding more defenders, and better defenders, over the summer? The reason I think we’ll all get over this week quickly is because Barcelona, at the end of the day, are a great team, and much better than Real Madrid when fully fit. I don’t mean to sound like a sore loser, I’m just calling a spade a spade. Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde will be back soon. The games this week were the toughest tests of the first half of the season. Barcelona has time to learn from the mistakes they made in these two very disappointing losses. More than anything, my frustration lies with the work, or lack there of, that was done in the summer transfer window. Can this be remedied in January? If Barcelona want to repeat as Spanish champions, and be more serious as contenders in the Champions League, then my conclusion now is that they must add depth defensively. Flick’s tactics work, but they are also very demanding, and he needs to be able to rotate at every position, and know that he won’t experience a big drop in quality. Right now, the defenders represent a big vulnerability. Jose Mourinho understands Barcelona well. He is the ultimate boogeyman, because he knows how to use his opponents’ strengths against them. His is the perfect foil to the beautiful way Barcelona insists on playing. Take this week as a dose of realism. In football, often times, the better team doesn’t win. When you’re up against an antagonist, take note, and be smart. Hansi Flick has some important takeaways, but so do Deco and Joan Laporta. I expect Barcelona to get back on track quickly, but come Springtime they must be better prepared. That means being more flexible tactically, but also having the necessary depth of talent to navigate a demanding calendar. Teams like Real Madrid prioritize winning above all else, no matter how it happens. Accordingly, Barcelona must not be naïve. This season just got real. Scoring lots of goals is wonderful, but defense will always win championships. PSG and Real Madrid are very different teams, but both taught Barcelona this harsh lesson. Barcelona must be better defensively, and in order to do that, aside from tactics, they need the right personnel. If nothing changes, Barcelona are rolling the dice, and that simply is unacceptable.

item.title: PAK vs ENG: Drama in Lahore! Shadab Khan walks off, England celebrate, then comes a twist - WATCH
item.description: NEW DELHI: For a few moments at Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium, it seemed Pakistan had lost the match. England's players had started celebrating, handshakes were exchanged and Shadab Khan looked devastated. But a review changed everything, and the hosts went on to pull off a stunning one-wicket victory in the ODI tri-series on Sunday. Pakistan were chasing 242 and had slipped to 154-9. With just one wicket left, defeat looked certain. Then Shadab and Haris Rauf produced a remarkable fightback, taking Pakistan home and securing their place in the final. Shadab remained unbeaten on 113, but his innings had one moment that could have ended the contest before its dramatic finish. Shadab walks away, but the review saves Pakistan The drama unfolded in the 45th over when Gus Atkinson trapped Shadab on the pads. The bowler appealed, and the umpire raised his finger. Shadab appeared to accept his fate and began walking away. England's players thought they had won. Some started shaking hands, while the television briefly flashed a result showing England winning by 20 runs. Shadab was clearly upset. He struck his bat against the ground and went down on his haunches. Joe Root and Harry Brook approached him to shake hands as other England players began celebrating. — lenphil29 (@lenphil29) But Shadab decided to review the decision, and the replays changed the mood inside the stadium. UltraEdge showed a spike, confirming that the ball had touched his bat before hitting his pad. The decision was overturned, and the crowd erupted. Shadab was given another chance to finish the match, while England's players looked stunned. Rauf, who had put his hand on his head during the tense moment, also watched in disbelief. Shadab responded with a fist pump. Pakistan's hopes were alive again, and the match continued. Shadab and Rauf pull off an incredible comeback When Rauf joined Shadab in the 34th over, Pakistan were struggling at 154-9. England needed only one more wicket, but the last pair refused to surrender. Shadab took responsibility for the chase, scoring quickly and protecting Rauf from facing too many deliveries. He kept most of the strike and continued to put pressure on England's bowlers. Playing his first match of the tournament, Shadab smashed 113 not out off 96 balls, with 12 fours and five sixes. Rauf supported him with an unbeaten seven off 19 deliveries. Their 89-run partnership was the highest for the 10th wicket in a successful ODI run chase. Shadab brought up his maiden ODI century with a late cut off Atkinson and followed it with a six over long-off. Pakistan needed only three runs from the final three overs when Rauf struck the winning boundary off Henry Crocombe. Pakistan finished on 243-9 in 47.1 overs to complete a victory few would have expected when their ninth wicket fell. — CallMeSheri1_ (@CallMeSheri1_) Afridi strikes early as England are bowled out for 241 Earlier, England were dismissed for 241 in 46.4 overs after being asked to bat first. Ben Duc

Pakistan finished on 243-9 in 47.1 overs to complete a victory few would have expected when their ninth wicket fell. — CallMeSheri1_ (@CallMeSheri1_) Afridi strikes early as England are bowled out for 241 Earlier, England were dismissed for 241 in 46.4 overs after being asked to bat first. Ben Duckett top-scored with 105 off 111 balls, hitting 10 fours and two sixes. Shaheen Shah Afridi put England under pressure from the start. He dismissed Tom Banton in the first over and Joe Root in the third, before Rauf removed Jordan Cox. England were soon reduced to 52-4. Duckett and Sam Curran then gave the innings some stability, adding 93 runs for the fifth wicket. Curran scored 42 off 52 balls before Afridi dismissed him, completing his third wicket of the innings. Afridi finished with 4-46 as England continued to lose wickets. They slipped to 201-9 before Gus Atkinson, who remained unbeaten on 36, helped them reach 241. Despite Duckett's century and Atkinson's late contribution, England's total was not enough to stop Pakistan's remarkable chase. England come close, but Pakistan survive Pakistan also struggled with the bat. Fakhar Zaman and Babar Azam scored 10 each, while Saim Ayub managed only six. Jamie Overton took two catches in the slips to dismiss Fakhar and Saim, while Atkinson bowled Babar. Saad Baig added a quick 32 off 22 balls, and Salman Ali Agha scored 26. But England continued to take wickets, with Overton finishing with 3-43 and Liam Dawson claiming 2-30. At 154-9, England were firmly in control. However, Shadab's counter-attack, Rauf's support and the crucial review turned the match on its head. Pakistan book a place in the final The victory secured Pakistan's place in the ODI tri-series final. They will play Sri Lanka in their last league match on Tuesday, having beaten them by 37 runs in the opening game. England, meanwhile, suffered their third consecutive defeat. They had earlier lost to Pakistan by 87 runs and then suffered a heartbreaking loss against Sri Lanka, who chased down 430 with one ball remaining.

item.title: Valverde played over 40 minutes injured as Real Madrid face three away games in a week
item.description: Valverde played over 40 minutes injured as Real Madrid face three away games in a week Real Madrid came away from Camp Nou on Sunday night with three points and a new fitness worry. José Mourinho revealed after the 2-1 win over Barcelona that Fede Valverde had spent a large part of the game carrying an injury, and the timing is far from ideal with three away fixtures to come in the space of seven days. The coach went out of his way to single out the Uruguayan in his post-match press conference , saying Valverde “played injured for more than 40 minutes”. Mourinho added: “He got injured, wanted to continue, pushed himself to his limits, and gave everything while he was on the field.” No details yet on Valverde’s problem Mourinho did not say what kind of injury Valverde had suffered or at what point in the match it happened. At the time of writing, Real Madrid had not published a medical report on the midfielder, who was named in the starting XI alongside Aurélien Tchouaméni, Bernardo Silva and Jude Bellingham. The club’s English account still made him one of the faces of the night, sharing a Valverde post shortly after midnight. Lunin answers the call as Courtois misses out Valverde was not the only fitness story of the weekend. Thibaut Courtois dropped out on matchday because of what the club called a flu-like illness , with Illia Voloshyn called up as cover. Andriy Lunin started in goal and, according to Real Madrid’s own match report, made a fine stop from a Gerard Martín header in the 66th minute. Mourinho said his only message to Lunin before kick-off was simple: “You train to play, not to sit on the bench. Go and play.” He also stressed that the squad had not been rattled by the late change, adding that “today none of us cried before the match because Thibaut wasn’t playing”. Courtois, whose future has been discussed in terms of a possible one-year contract extension , now has a few days to recover before the next game. Three trips in a week The calendar offers Madrid little breathing space. Mourinho pointed out that “on Sunday we play away; then we play away on Wednesday, and then we have another away match on Saturday”. According to the fixture list , those games are against Racing Santander on 1 November, AEK Athens in the Champions League on 4 November and Valencia on 7 November. That run is where Mourinho’s faith in his squad will be tested. He insisted after the Clásico that “I have a rich bench, with players who can be starters”, and he backed it up at Camp Nou by leaving Eduardo Camavinga among the substitutes days after his strong display in the 4-1 win over RB Leipzig . Camavinga came on and set up the late winner for Kylian Mbappé. The victory was Madrid’s fifth in a row and, as Mourinho noted, leaves them three points behind Barcelona rather than six or nine. Keeping that momentum through three away games will be far easier with Valverde available, so the club’s next medical update on the midfielder will be closely watched before

item.title: Michael Carrick on the brink of Manchester United exit after Bournemouth humiliation
item.description: Michael Carrick on the brink of Manchester United exit after Bournemouth humiliation Michael Carrick is on the cusp of losing his job as Manchester United head coach after the humiliating 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth at Old Trafford, The Telegraph reports. The loss was United’s sixth in 12 games this season and left the club just one point above the Premier League relegation zone. It has also increased the pressure on Carrick as the club hierarchy considers their next move. United haven’t made a formal decision yet, but the 45-year-old is on thin ice and an immediate managerial change cannot be ruled out. United fans were fuming after the game, but channelled their frustration toward co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, director of football Jason Wilcox, and the players. After the match, Carrick admitted he understood the pressure on his position but insisted he would keep working until a decision was made. “I totally understand the situation,” he said. “I’m not expecting anything either way. I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. “I’ll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, and I won’t change that now, whatever decision is made. “It’s a tough situation, there’s no hiding from it. What it looks like and what’s next I really don’t know. “I love what I do, and I feel the responsibility – we’ll have to wait and see. I take responsibility. I respect the position that I’m in, and the responsibility is mine. What else can I say really right now?” Tensions have also grown between Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes . The midfielder was left out of the starting line-up after criticising the manager’s tactics following Wednesday’s 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como. Carrick also chose not to bring Fernandes on against Bournemouth. Despite the club’s miserable form, United supporters showed their support for Carrick. They chanted his name during the match before directing their anger at the club’s leadership and players at full time. Antonio Conte is one of several managers named as potential replacements for Carrick. Former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe is also in the mix .

item.title: Aaron Rodgers hints NFL owners shut down original plans for International Week to avoid spending
item.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images In typical Aaron Rodgers fashion, the former MVP has put NFL owners on blast while discussing the original plan for the league’s international expansion. Rodgers has definitely earned his reputation for being one of the most polarising, controversial, and outspoken figures in the history of the NFL. But his latest comments might draw the ire of the NFL’s top brass, as he might be revealing secrets the leadership don’t want to be known. Aaron Rodgers claimed ‘greedy’ NFL owners pushed for 17th game over International Week Speaking to reporters ahead of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris, Aaron Rodgers addressed the NFL’s original expansion plans. Rodgers revealed that during an earlier Collective Bargaining Agreement negotiation, the NFL considered an entire slate of international games for one week, but the owners shut it down as they wanted to play more games and didn’t want to invest more to expand internationally. Rodgers said: “We didn’t really have a lot till the second CBA, and there was talk of doing an International Week where you had games in 16 different places and just added an extra bye week. So you would play 16 regular-season games and two bye weeks. One of those bye weeks would have been International Week. “I think it would have been phenomenal for the game, now that the owners want to push for 17 games for the extra revenue, and because they care so much about player safety (sarcastically). It would have been nice. I think there are 16 opportunities. “I think you could do Canada, Mexico, there have been games in Brazil, you could probably open up another country in South America, and obviously there are a lot of opportunities in Europe… Then who knows? Obviously, there’s Dubai in that area that has really taken to the sporting world in a number of ways… “There are great opportunities for expansion, and it’ll be awesome to have an International Week, because I think it is great for the expansion of the game. “I wish there was a mandate, though, from the league, and they would have to open up their pocketbooks too, which maybe they’re tight on money and stuff, but I think they should mandate every team coming over Sunday or Monday… But they won’t because they are tight.” The NFL has made international expansion one of their top priorities going forward, but it is hard to understand why owners would push more for an extra game. Any revenue they would earn from an additional game would be more in the short term, but expanding the NFL’s presence globally could secure more long-term revenue streams from outside of the United States. item.title: Kathleen Krüger reflects on Bayern Munich’s bad luck with Vincent Kompany, Joshua Kimmich
item.description: 19 September 2026, Hamburg: Soccer, Men: Bundesliga, Hamburger SV vs. 1. FC Köln, Matchday 4, at Volksparkstadion,Kathleen Krüger, Chief Sports Officer of HSV Fußball AG, before kickoff. Photo: Marcus Brandt/dpa - IMPORTANT NOTICE: In accordance with the regulations of the Bundesliga and the DFB (German Football Association), it is prohibited to use or allow the use of photographs taken in the stadium and/or during the game in the form of sequential images and/or video-like photo series. (Photo by Marcus Brandt/picture alliance via Getty Images) Former Bayern Munich player and team manager Kathleen Krüger, once described as the most powerful woman in the Bundesliga, reflected on the current situation that the club is going through, feeling the losses of Joshua Kimmich and Vincent Kompany—both through extremely unfortunate circumstances. Speaking in an interview captured by @iMiaSanMia , Krüger was emotional when touching on the topics of Kompany and Kimmich. “I think the entire week at FC Bayern has been an intense one—not so much on the sporting side, but actually on a very human level. When I think about Joshua Kimmich and his whole family, for example, it’s obviously devastating, and it affects me deeply. I’m thinking very, very much a bout him and his entire family, and now also about Vinnie, and of course I really hope he gets much, m uch better very quickly,” she said. The now-sporting director at H amburg SV has a deep connection to the club, having been active within the system for almost 20 years. With Bayern missing players like Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala, and Kim Min-jae, it’s hard to focus on the positives, but the club remains optimistic. Bayern Munich is indeed going through a rough patch, and no institution should have to hit this kind of bump. All fans can do is hope for the best for both players and all the others currently injured.

item.title: Andy Reid Gives True Thoughts on Chiefs Losing to Seahawks
item.description: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs offense had no answer for the Seattle Seahawks’ defense as the reigning Super Bowl champions secured a 20-3 win on Oct. 25 at Lumen Field. Kansas City’s running game with Kenneth Walker III was a nonfactor as he only recorded 36 rushing yards. With no run game to lean on, Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes couldn’t get much going in the passing attack. Mahomes went 19-for-33 on his passing attempts for 165 passing yards, recording one interception and a passer rating of 58.3. After the loss to Seattle, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid spoke to the media and shared his thoughts on what went wrong for his team. “All three phases, we struggled,” Reid told reporters . “So we’ve got to do better, and that’s my responsibility. I take full responsibility for this. We’ve got to play better as a team. Tough place to play, but this is all part of it. They got their good football. They played well. My hat goes off to them. “There’s not a whole lot of stats that I can share with you that really make any sense, maybe other than third downs on both sides of the ball. We can do a better job with those, but we’ve got a great locker room here, and guys will get back in and get themselves ready to play against a good Denver team this next week.” Chiefs Have to Learn From Loss to Seahawks Moreover, Reid noted that the Chiefs need to learn from this game as the Seahawks are one of, if not the best, defenses that his team will face this season. “We’ve got to learn from it,” Reid added . “I mentioned to you guys before, win or lose, you’ve got to learn and get better. We’ll all do that. I’ll start with myself, and we’ll work our way through it and make sure that we teach. item.title: Titans’ Cam Ward gives bizarre reason for brutal miss late in Browns game
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Titans’ Cam Ward gives bizarre reason for brutal miss late in Browns game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tennessee Titans found themselves locked in a tight late-game battle against the Cleveland Browns, needing every play to go right. But when quarterback Cam Ward had a wide-open receiver staring him down in the clutch, things took an unexpected turn, and his postgame explanation was just as candid as the missed throw. Late in the fourth quarter, Ward spotted tight end Daniel Bellinger breaking open down the seam. It was the exact look Tennessee had dialed up, but Ward ended up sailing the pass well over Bellinger’s head, squandering a massive chunk-play opportunity. Speaking to reporters after the game, Ward didn’t blame bad footwork or a miscommunication. Instead, he admitted pure excitement got the best of him. Ward explained that the team had been waiting all afternoon to catch Cleveland in Tampa 2 coverage. When the defensive safety split and the gap opened precisely as designed, he got so hyped seeing the open grass that he completely overshot his target. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cam Ward said they finally got the coverage they wanted (Tampa 2) on Daniel Bellinger's seam route late and he got excited causing him to overshoot. Ward said next play mentality led to redemption on passes to Elic Ayomanor and Carnell Tate a few plays later. pic.twitter.com/hIKRotgF5R — TURRON DAVENPORT (@TDavenport_NFL) October 25, 2026 It was a bizarrely honest admission from a young signal-caller, especially on a day where passing production was hard to come by. Ward struggled to find rhythm against Cleveland’s defense, finishing the afternoon 15-of-29 passing for 142 yards and an interception while taking three sacks. Fortunately for the Titans, the brutal miss didn’t break Ward’s composure for long. Relying on a quick “next play mentality,” he bounced right back on the very same drive. Ward flushed the error, regrouped in the huddle, and delivered clutch completions to wide receivers Elic Ayomanor and Carnell Tate a few plays later to move the chains and keep the drive alive. While overshooting a target because you got overly excited isn’t ideal, Ward’s ability to shake off mistakes on the fly shows real maturity. Learning to stay cool when defenses give him the coverage he wants will be his next big step. Related: Titans’ Robert Saleh refuses to admit he has a Cam Ward problem despite calling out bad misses Related: Titans’ Robert Saleh gets real about Alontae Taylor position change ahead of Browns matchup

item.title: Hansi Flick blames 'lack of freshness' as Barcelona's winning streak ends in El Clasico defeat
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Hansi Flick has urged his Barcelona squad to refocus following a painful late defeat in the Clasico, which ended their perfect start to the Liga campaign. The German manager expressed frustration over his team's lack of freshness and highlighted mounting injury problems as his primary concern moving forward. Barcelona suffer painful late Clasico defeat Barca's flawless start to the Liga season under Flick has officially come to a disappointing end. The Catalan club finally dropped their first points of the domestic campaign following a painful Clasico defeat . A decisive blow in the closing minutes proved to be their undoing, stripping Blaugrana of their perfect league record. The 2-1 defeat brings an abrupt halt to a highly impressive nine-match winning streak in the Spanish top flight. Crucially, the late heartbreak also condemns the team to their second consecutive defeat overall, testing their early-season resolve. Flick highlights details and lack of freshness Flick was quick to assess the underlying reasons behind the frustrating result. The Barca manager openly admitted his team fell short of their usual physical standards in such a highly demanding fixture. He acknowledged that minor margins dictate the outcome of high-profile encounters. "We're disappointed because we lacked freshness," the German coach explained on the club's official website . "It's our first defeat in La Liga after nine consecutive wins, but these things happen. In big games, the details are very important, and today they didn't go our way. Defeats are part of football. We have to analyse what happened, do things better, and that's what we'll do." Injuries become biggest concern for Barca Beyond the obvious disappointment of the final scoreline, the club's mounting medical list is causing significant headaches. Barca unfortunately lost yet another defender during the clash as Xavi Espart suffered a fresh issue. Flick made absolutely no secret of his profound worries regarding the current squad fitness levels. He admitted frankly that "the injuries are the biggest concern" for the coaching staff right now. Despite the defensive blow, the match did provide one major positive boost for the midfield engine room. Frenkie de Jong finally returned to competitive action, with Flick noting: "He's trained very well and will be useful to us." Squad must refocus and react to setbacks Barca must now find a way to bounce back immediately from this difficult period. Facing two consecutive defeats, the immediate pressure is on the dressing room to quickly halt this sudden slide in momentum. Blaugrana will next face Alaves in Liga this weekend, before hosting Aston Villa in the Champions League.

item.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Start time, odds, how to watch and nominations in full
item.description: The Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place tonight with a men’s and women’s winner set to be announced in London on Monday 26 October. England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is the favourite, with Spain and Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal a close second as debate swirls around the biggest individual prize in the sport. Kane is aiming to be the first English player to win the men’s award since Michael Owen in 2001, despite lacking a continental trophy, with the 33-year-old’s gluttony for goals and assists positioning him nicely to secure a career-high honour. Rodri , the Ballon d’Or winner in 2024, won the golden ball at the World Cup after leading Spain to glory while France and Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe broke the World Cup goalscoring record after hitting an incredible 10 goals across the tournament. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who has since suffered a season-ending knee injury was absent from the World Cup but was arguably the standout player in the men’s Champions League last season after inspiring back-to-back titles for Paris Saint-Germain. When is the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony? The Ballon d’Or ceremony will take place in London on Monday, 26 October , with the event getting underway from 8pm GMT . You can watch the ceremony on the official website ballondor.com or DAZN , globally, with a free live stream available from both, while Independent Sport will bring you a live blog with updates, reaction and analysis. According to Ball, there can be a memorable consequence for looking elsewhere. His explanation involved a laugh, an unusual teaching method and a lesson he learned growing up. Asked how he taught his teammates to be ready for his passes, Ball offered an answer that should entertain Minnesota fans. There was no complicated breakdown of timing or positioning. His approach sounded more direct. Timberwolves’ LaMelo Ball Explains His Unusual Passing Lesson “Nah, just get your head up,” Ball said in an interview shared by Andrew Dukowitz. “Actually, I tried to hit them in the head a couple times.” Ball laughed while explaining the idea, making the playful nature of his comments important to the context. He was discussing how teammates learn to anticipate the basketball. According to Ball, there can be a memorable consequence for looking elsewhere. His explanation involved a laugh, an unusual teaching method and a lesson he learned growing up. Asked how he taught his teammates to be ready for his passes, Ball offered an answer that should entertain Minnesota fans. There was no complicated breakdown of timing or positioning. His approach sounded more direct. Timberwolves’ LaMelo Ball Explains His Unusual Passing Lesson “Nah, just get your head up,” Ball said in an interview shared by Andrew Dukowitz. “Actually, I tried to hit them in the head a couple times.” Ball laughed while explaining the idea, making the playful nature of his comments important to the context. He was discussing how teammates learn to anticipate the basketball. His next words connected that approach to his own childhood experience. “Once you get that in the head one time, you’re always gonna have your head up,” Ball said. “That’s how I was as a kid.” The delivery makes this an entertaining quote, but there is a basketball point underneath it. A passer can recognize an opening before the intended receiver realizes the ball is coming. If that teammate is watching something else, the opportunity can disappear before a shot becomes possible. Getty MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 05: LaMelo Ball #1 of the Minnesota Timberwolves dribbles the ball against the Milwaukee Bucks in the first quarter during the preseason NBA game at Fiserv Forum on October 05, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) That is where Minnesota’s adjustment becomes interesting. Playing alongside a creative distributor requires more than waiting for a familiar action to develop. Teammates have to remain available even when they do not appear to be the obvious option. Why LaMelo Ball Wants Minnesota Teammates Ready for Every Pass Ball’s explanation puts some responsibility on the receiving end of the partnership. Fans focus on the player delivering an impressive pass. However, the teammate catching it must recognize the moment and be prepared to finish the possession. For the Timberwolves, that is the useful takeaway beyond the punchline. An unexpected pass only creates an advantage if the receiver can do something with it. Catching the ball cleanly helps preserve the opening instead of giving defenders time to recover. That does not mean every possession needs to become a highlight. Sometimes the value comes from a teammate being ready for a simple pass delivered earlier than expected. Awareness can make an ordinary opportunity easier to convert. Ball did not present his comments as a complaint about Minnesota’s players. The laughter and childhood reference gave the exchange a lighter tone. Turning it into evidence of frustration would stretch the interview beyond what he said. The quote is memorable because the teaching method sounds ridiculous. The underlying instruction is familiar to anyone who has played basketball. Around Ball, Minnesota’s players have another reason to keep watching for the next pass. The NBA world certainly always finds the time to appreciate a Ball quote. item.title: Creaking, smug … and a contender? Aaron Rodgers may yet get his Super Bowl farewell
item.description: Aaron Rodgers and Cameron Heyward walk off the field after Sunday’s win. Photograph: Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers is nowhere near this season’s MVP conversation. At times in his second season with the Steelers, the almost 43-year-old has shown glimpses of the player he was in his prime, slinging the ball with zest and precision, able to suss out any coverage. Other times he has looked like, well, a guy in his 40s playing a young man’s game. Rodgers looked more like prime Rodgers in the Steelers’ gritty 16-10 win over the Saints in Paris. He wasn’t satisfied with his side of the ball, telling reporter Molly McGrath, “I don’t think we played very good on offense today.” But Rodgers did enough to secure the win, including a 51-yard strike to DK Metcalf in the second quarter. He later scrambled for a first down on third-and-six to secure the win. Sure, there were points left on the table – the Steelers had several stalled drives and only scored one touchdown in four red-zone trips – and 16 points against a two-win team isn’t impressive. But the Steelers left France with a win, a 5-2 record and a ton of upside. So here’s a crazy thought: Could Rodgers win a Super Bowl in his final NFL season? But when you consider the parts around Rodgers, perhaps it’s not so crazy. As competent as Rodgers was against the Saints, the defense stole the show. They smothered Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, and shut down the Saints run game as Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen had predicted. This Steelers run defense is punishing and only improving. In Weeks 1-4, they allowed 4.5 yards per carry. Over the last three weeks, it has dropped to 2.8 yards per carry. All told, Pittsburgh’s defense has allowed just three touchdowns in the last 15 quarters. That is some 2025 Seahawks-level domination. Offensively, Rodgers is no worse than Sam Darnold was last year when the Seahawks won the Super Bowl. He’s thrown 13 touchdowns and five interceptions for 1,699 yards through his first seven games this season – Darnold had 12 TDs, four picks and 1,754 yards over the same span in 2025.
