item.content:encoded: Aaron Rodgers and Cameron Heyward walk off the field after Sunday’s win. Photograph: Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers is nowhere near this season’s MVP conversation. At times in his second season with the Steelers, the almost 43-year-old has shown glimpses of the player he was in his prime, slinging the ball with zest and precision, able to suss out any coverage. Other times he has looked like, well, a guy in his 40s playing a young man’s game. Rodgers looked more like prime Rodgers in the Steelers’ gritty 16-10 win over the Saints in Paris. He wasn’t satisfied with his side of the ball, telling reporter Molly McGrath, “I don’t think we played very good on offense today.” But Rodgers did enough to secure the win, including a 51-yard strike to DK Metcalf in the second quarter. He later scrambled for a first down on third-and-six to secure the win. Sure, there were points left on the table – the Steelers had several stalled drives and only scored one touchdown in four red-zone trips – and 16 points against a two-win team isn’t impressive. But the Steelers left France with a win, a 5-2 record and a ton of upside. So here’s a crazy thought: Could Rodgers win a Super Bowl in his final NFL season? But when you consider the parts around Rodgers, perhaps it’s not so crazy. As competent as Rodgers was against the Saints, the defense stole the show. They smothered Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, and shut down the Saints run game as Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen had predicted. This Steelers run defense is punishing and only improving. In Weeks 1-4, they allowed 4.5 yards per carry. Over the last three weeks, it has dropped to 2.8 yards per carry. All told, Pittsburgh’s defense has allowed just three touchdowns in the last 15 quarters. That is some 2025 Seahawks-level domination. Offensively, Rodgers is no worse than Sam Darnold was last year when the Seahawks won the Super Bowl. He’s thrown 13 touchdowns and five interceptions for 1,699 yards through his first seven games this season – Darnold had 12 TDs, four picks and 1,754 yards over the same span in 2025. Saints linebacker Kaden Elliss likened Rodgers to a point guard, noting the advantage he has over other NFL quarterbacks. “Even though he’s up there in age, I think that’s an advantage to him, his mind,” Elliss said after Sunday’s game. “And I think he used that today.” Maybe Rodgers’s football IQ could catapult Pittsburgh to a deep playoff run in the AFC. Yes, there are the perennial Super Bowl contenders like Kansas City and Buffalo, but no AFC team this season is a winning machine like the Patriots in the Brady-Belichick era. And, after a ho-hum Super Bowl from a star power perspective, a Rodgers return to the big stage would set off fireworks. Of course, Rodgers comes with plenty of baggage due to his commitment to his “own research” during Covid, his ridiculous antipathy towards Anthony Fauci and his habit of calling out coaches and teammates. Recently, though, he appears to have realized keeping his opinions to himself is probably the best course of action. His worst take over the weekend was appearing to think Peaky Blinders was set in France rather than England . He’s not exactly likable, but considering what he’s said in the past, his recent behavior seems like progress. Not that he’s completely quiet. In Paris, when asked about the International Series, he let it be known that team owners had considered a 16-game schedule with an entire international week, where teams play all over the world and two byes. Instead, according to Rodgers , they opted for the 17-game schedule to rake in extra cash. Rodgers added that the league “may be a little tight on money,” a refreshing level of shade that will win him some fans. Realistically, Rodgers and the Steelers will need a good deal of luck to make it to the Super Bowl this year. But that’s the case for plenty of teams. A run to the title game would send Rodgers’s smugness of the charts, but you have to admit that his final game coming on Super Bowl Sunday would be interesting. MVP of the week Joe Burrow, QB, Cincinnati Bengals. Down 13-0 at the half, the Bengals looked destined for an infuriating loss, an art they specialize in. They had mustered just 49 passing yards, and were struggling to sustain drives. Meanwhile, the supposedly retooled Bengals defense couldn’t get the Ravens off the field. At the half, Baltimore, led by a backup quarterback, had dominated the time of possession 22:20 to 7:40. Yet again, Cincinnati looked like a fringe playoff team not meeting their full potential. And after locking up star receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins for Joe Burrow in his prime, being a fringe playoff team isn’t acceptable. Chase’s halftime team talk seems to have worked. “I told our offense [that] we can’t look at our defense the whole time. We’ve got to step this shit up and make something work,” he said after the game. Burrow, who is chasing his first league MVP, duly played out of his mind. He was essentially perfect after the break, dicing up the Ravens secondary for four touchdowns on four drives with 243 yards and an 89% completion percentage. Burrow made it look effortless as he tends to do at his best. Stat of the week 64 . How do the Bucs win a game 43-13 when Baker Mayfield only throws 64 passing yards? They faced a Panthers team who were a walking comedy of errors. Mayfield only threw 11 passes in his first game back from dislocating his thumb, and did connect with Tez Johnson for a score. The damage unsurprisingly came on the ground – Tampa rushed for 258 yards and three touchdowns, including two from Bucky Irving, who eclipsed 100 yards. The Bucs also strip-sacked Bryce Young and returned it for a touchdown. Imagine the score if Mayfield was slinging the rock. Video of the week Bo Nix came into Sunday’s game with just 37 rushing yards all season. So when the Broncos quarterback nearly doubled that total in one play – a 62-yard touchdown run that gave Denver a late second-quarter lead over Arizona – hell yeah, he was going to add a flourish. The spin move at the goalline may not have been necessary, but it must have been cathartic. Nix has been criticized for not providing an offensive spark, even though Denver came into the game at 4-2 after negotiating one of the league’s toughest schedules. But Nix looked far more comfortable – and at times electric – in Sunday’s 30-16 win. He finished with the one long rushing touchdown, and 222 passing yards. Elsewhere around the league -- The Chiefs were undefeated going into their game with the Super Bowl champion Seahawks but we knew Kansas City had flaws. Patrick Mahomes has been good rather than great, the receiving corps is ravaged and their schedule had been soft to start the season. On Sunday Night Football, they were overwhelmed by Seattle, whose defense became the first unit this season to make former Seahawk Kenneth Walker III look human. And Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba was terrifying once again, hauling in 150 receiving yards in his team’s 20-3 win. “One hell of a game from Sam Darnold,” said Smith-Njigba, slightly underplaying his own contribution. –- The Dolphins are no longer winless after humiliating the Jets 28-25 at MetLife. Geno Smith was outplayed by Malik Willis, who played clean football and was able to scramble at will, especially in the first half. Jeff Hafley outcoached Aaron Glenn, not a hard feat. Given New York’s talent advantage, they have no business losing at home to a 0-5 team with severe salary cap issues. But when the Dolphins have the ball for the final nine minutes of the first half and Glenn enters the break with all three timeouts remaining, winning is difficult. The Jets’ star receiver, Garrett Wilson, has cut a frustrated figure recently and was only targeted three times on Sunday. CBS cameras caught him yelling on the sidelines, although he later denied his anger was directed at his quarterback, Geno Smith. “We were collaboratin

item.title: Real Madrid legend praises Jose Mourinho’s tactical approach after Barcelona victory
item.description: Real Madrid legend praises Jose Mourinho’s tactical approach after Barcelona victory Real Madrid secured an important 2-1 victory over Barcelona in the league’s first El Clasico at the Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday night. It was a game Jose Mourinho went into with a point to prove, and he got his starting XI and tactics spot on. Real Madrid legend Iker Casillas has now praised Jose Mourinho following the victory, highlighting the Portuguese manager’s tactical approach. Casillas applauds Mourinho’s El Clasico tactics In a tweet on X, the former Madrid goalkeeper expressed his satisfaction with his old club’s performance and reserved particular praise for the coach. “This is La Liga! Very good from Real Madrid. A very good tactical approach from Mourinho,” Casillas wrote. The endorsement carries additional significance given the complicated relationship between the two during Mourinho’s previous spell in charge of Madrid. Despite their past differences, Casillas was quick to recognise the manager’s contribution to an important victory over Barcelona. Madrid entered the encounter six points behind Hansi Flick’s side, making the trip to the Camp Nou particularly significant in the title race. The visitors responded with a disciplined performance, securing three points and reducing the gap to just three. Mourinho’s approach pays off against Barcelona Madrid’s performance was built around competing aggressively in midfield and making their attacking opportunities count. Jude Bellingham’s remarkable 13 successful duels illustrated the intensity Mourinho’s players brought to the contest. The visitors also had to overcome the late absence of Thibaut Courtois , with Andriy Lunin stepping in after the Belgian goalkeeper fell ill. Real Madrid outclassed Barcelona at the Spotify Camp Nou. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Despite some circumstances working against them, Los Blancos managed to emerge more prepared than their opponents. Madrid showed the organisation and competitive edge required to overcome a Barcelona side that had enjoyed an impressive start to the season. The challenge now is to reproduce that intensity consistently, particularly against opponents who present different tactical problems. They are still three points behind Barça , and having done the difficult job of closing the gap, they should not let it widen again. Los Blancos have positioned themselves right in the mix for the title once again, and it remains to be seen how they fare in the upcoming games.

item.title: Lecce-Juventus | Standout Stats
item.description: Lecce-Juventus | Standout Stats The key facts and figures from Juventus' Serie A clash against Lecce, including the standout numbers from the Bianconeri's individual performances. UNBEATEN AGAINST LECCE Juventus are unbeaten in their last 13 Serie A meetings with Lecce, recording nine wins and four draws, with an aggregate score of 21-6. SOLID ON THE ROAD Juventus have kept six clean sheets in their last nine Serie A away matches, one more than the five they managed in their previous 25 away league fixtures played in 2026. MCKENNIE BACK ON THE SCORESHEET Weston McKennie scored his first Serie A goal since 6 April 2026, when he found the net against Genoa at the Allianz Stadium. The American had gone 10 league appearances without scoring and 18 away matches in the competition without a goal. MCKENNIE MAKES HIS MARK Weston McKennie ended a run of 819 minutes without a goal involvement in Serie A. His previous contribution came on 19 April 2026, when he provided the assist for Khéphren Thuram's goal against Bologna. WESTON'S NUMBERS Among the players currently in the Juventus squad, Weston McKennie has the most goal involvements across all competitions, with 54 (28 goals and 26 assists), followed by Kenan Yildiz on 43. A FIRST FOR DOUGLAS LUIZ For the first time in his career, Douglas Luiz both scored and provided an assist in the same match across Europe's top five leagues, having previously made 261 appearances in those competitions. DOUGLAS LUIZ'S CONTRIBUTION Douglas Luiz has been directly involved in two goals in eight Serie A appearances this season, scoring once and providing one assist. The Brazilian did not register a goal or an assist in his 19 league appearances for Juventus during the 2024/25 campaign. SECOND-HALF PRESSURE Juventus attempted 12 shots in the second half against Lecce, three times as many as the four they registered in the opening 45 minutes. BREMER REACHES 200 Bremer made his 200th Serie A start against Lecce.

item.title: Frenkie de Jong explains why Barcelona struggled against Real Madrid in El Clasico: ‘We weren’t as fluid as usual’
item.description: Frenkie de Jong explains why Barcelona struggled against Real Madrid in El Clasico: ‘We weren’t as fluid as usual’ Frenkie de Jong has outlined Barcelona’s shortcomings after returning to action in their 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid in the first El Clasico of the 2026/27 season, admitting that Hansi Flick’s side lacked their usual fluency in possession. The Dutch midfielder also made his ambition clear, insisting he wants to reclaim a place in Barcelona’s starting XI as quickly as possible. Joao Cancelo, meanwhile, argued that Barcelona were the better team despite losing at home, while acknowledging that their inability to control possession consistently proved costly against Real Madrid. De Jong identifies Barcelona’s costly mistakes De Jong returned to the pitch against Real Madrid but could not help Barcelona avoid defeat in a disappointing result at Spotify Camp Nou. The midfielder admitted that losing El Clasico at home made the setback particularly painful, especially after a difficult week for the Catalan club. “It always hurts to lose, especially at home and especially in El Clásico. It’s not what we expected, but we’re top of the table and we have to bounce back after this rotten week .” Frenkie de Jong played his first match for Barcelona this season. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The Dutchman also explained how Barcelona’s mistakes in possession played into Madrid’s strengths, allowing their opponents to threaten quickly after winning the ball. “It’s true we weren’t as fluid as usual; we lost possession a bit more, and that’s their strength: if you lose the ball in the first or second phase of play, they have players who are very decisive and very quick .” Frenkie de Jong wants to reclaim starting place De Jong also addressed the competition for places in Barcelona’s midfield, where several high-quality options are fighting for regular minutes. Rather than viewing that competition negatively, the midfielder described it as a natural part of playing for a club with Barcelona’s ambitions. “We’ve got a lot of top-class players; there are some very good players in midfield in particular. Joao Cancelo has asked for more after Real Madrid defeat. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “Competition for places is to be expected in a team like Barcelona – it’s nothing new – and I want to contribute and get back into the starting eleven as quickly as possible.” Cancelo insists Barcelona were the better team Cancelo, on the other hand, offered a more assertive assessment of Barcelona’s performance, arguing that the result did not accurately reflect how the match unfolded from his perspective. “We were the better side in my view, but this is Real Madrid – they create few chances and still score against you. Overall, we were the better team.” However, the Portuguese defender also acknowledged that Barcelona needed greater control with the ball rather than relying too heavily on their high press. “We lacked a bit in that we often want to press

item.title: ‘Not Paying Enough Attention’ — Spurs Star Victor Wembanyama Admits Glaring Offensive Flaw After Being Denied in Back-to-Back Games
item.description: Collage featuring BASKETBALL-NBA-DAL-SAS/ and BASKETBALL-NBA-SAS-HOU/. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Victor Wembanyama has had his fair share of denials through the San Antonio Spurs’ first three games of the season. Most notable of those blocks came on consecutive nights last week, against the Houston Rockets and the Dallas Mavericks. Wembanyama, taking note of the uncharacteristic offensive hiccups, offered his own assessment of why his shots keep getting blocked. Spurs’ Star Victor Wembanyama Weighs in After Back-to-Back Rejections In the dying seconds of the Spurs’ designated home game against Houston at Moody Center in Austin, San Antonio trailed by two points with five seconds remaining. Wembanyama caught a pass in the paint and went up. Rockets guard Amen Thompson met him in midair and swatted away the would-be tying layup, and the Rockets held on for a 114-110 win. The 6-foot-7 Thompson finished with 20 points, 10 rebounds, and 2 blocks, while the 7-foot-4 Wembanyama had 25 points on 9-of-21 shooting and 13 rebounds. At his postgame press conference, the Spurs star was asked what he would have done differently on the final possession, and he kept it brief: “I would have dunked the ball.” There was little time to regroup, with a game in Dallas the next night. And once again, Zaccharie Risacher managed to swat Wembanyama’s shot away. DON’T MISS: ‘Waste of Height,’ ‘Needs to Drink More Creatine or Something’ — NBA Fans Baffled as Victor Wembanyama Gets Swatted in Back-to-Back Games San Antonio still pulled away for a 122-106 win over a Mavericks team playing without Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg, with Wembanyama posting 23 points, 7 rebounds, and 4 blocks in 29 minutes. Asked about the run of blocks, Wembanyama offered a candid self-assessment: “I think it’s a matter of not paying enough attention to where I am on the court, and where my opponents and teammates are.” The Spurs star also floated a second explanation: “Maybe I’m just rushing things.” Through three games, the 22-year-old has scored 60 points on 19-of-52 shooting from the field, including 4-of-16 from 3-point range. That works out to 20 points per game on 36.5% shooting. He is also averaging 11 rebounds and 4 blocks, and his 12 blocks are double the number of times his own shot has been blocked. Wembanyama’s percentage took its biggest hit in the season opener, a 116-104 home loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder on October 20. The visitors blocked 10 Spurs shots that night. Wembanyama went 1-of-13 from the field and leaned on a 10-of-12 showing at the free-throw line to finish with 12 points, along with 13 rebounds and 6 blocks. He has been more efficient since, shooting 18-of-39 over the next two games. The Spurs, who reached the NBA Finals last season, opened 0-2 before the win in Dallas lifted them to 1-2. Next up, San Antonio will return home to host the Sacramento Kings at Frost Bank Center on Tuesday. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: North Carolina HC Bill Belichick can’t find many words to describe unfathomable loss to Syracuse
item.description: Zachary Taft-Imagn Images North Carolina HC Bill Belichick can’t find many words to describe unfathomable loss to Syracuse appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coming off a victory over Duke , North Carolina football once again came up short, suffering 31-30 overtime loss against Syracuse. The narrow loss left head coach Bill Belichick with little to say as his team watched a promising opportunity slip away in the closing stages. item.title: ‘We Were the Better Side’: Peter Bosz Makes Feelings Clear After PSV 1-1 Feyenoord
item.description: PSV manager Peter Bosz believes his side can take confidence from their performances against FC Porto and Feyenoord, despite missing the opportunity to close the gap on the Eredivisie leaders after Sunday's 1-1 draw at the Philips Stadio n. Guus Til gave PSV the lead with a superb volley before half-time, but Anis Hadj-Moussa equalised after the break as Feyenoord recovered from a difficult opening period. PSV created further opportunities but failed to find a winner, leaving Bosz frustrated with the result. Nevertheless, the manager remained encouraged by his team's response following a difficult run of domestic results and their midweek Champions League victory over Porto. “We played with our heads held high, but we didn't win,” Bosz said after the match. “And yet, we have managed to draw confidence from this week.” Van Bommel had two opportunities to score but sent both efforts over the crossbar [IMAGO/ANP] Bosz Defends Decision To Start Van Bommel As Striker One of the notable decisions in Bosz's starting line-up was the deployment of Ruben van Bommel as the central striker . The 22-year-old had not previously played in that position, having typically operated on the left wing, but the PSV manager was pleased with his contribution. PSV have been without an established centre-forward option, and Bosz acknowledged that the absence of a natural striker might have affected his side's ability to convert their chances. “We don't have an out-and-out striker,” he explained. “Perhaps that plays a role, though I thought Ruben filled the position well today. We wanted to catch the opposition off guard, and I think we succeeded in that.” Bosz also outlined the tactical advantages of his decision, particularly the opportunity to preserve the partnership between Ivan Perisic and Filip Kostic. “There were several advantages to setting it up this way. For instance, it allowed the pairing of Ivan and Filip to remain intact. I also felt Ivan had an aerial advantage over Read,” he added. Van Bommel had two opportunities to score but sent both efforts over the crossbar. Despite his failure to convert, Bosz felt the chances themselves were encouraging. “As for Ruben, he had two chances, though he sent both shots over the bar. item.content:encoded: PSV manager Peter Bosz believes his side can take confidence from their performances against FC Porto and Feyenoord, despite missing the opportunity to close the gap on the Eredivisie leaders after Sunday's 1-1 draw at the Philips Stadio n. Guus Til gave PSV the lead with a superb volley before half-time, but Anis Hadj-Moussa equalised after the break as Feyenoord recovered from a difficult opening period. PSV created further opportunities but failed to find a winner, leaving Bosz frustrated with the result. Nevertheless, the manager remained encouraged by his team's response following a difficult run of domestic results and their midweek Champions League victory over Porto. “We played with our heads held high, but we didn't win,” Bosz said after the match. “And yet, we have managed to draw confidence from this week.” Van Bommel had two opportunities to score but sent both efforts over the crossbar [IMAGO/ANP] Bosz Defends Decision To Start Van Bommel As Striker One of the notable decisions in Bosz's starting line-up was the deployment of Ruben van Bommel as the central striker . The 22-year-old had not previously played in that position, having typically operated on the left wing, but the PSV manager was pleased with his contribution. PSV have been without an established centre-forward option, and Bosz acknowledged that the absence of a natural striker might have affected his side's ability to convert their chances. “We don't have an out-and-out striker,” he explained. “Perhaps that plays a role, though I thought Ruben filled the position well today. We wanted to catch the opposition off guard, and I think we succeeded in that.” Bosz also outlined the tactical advantages of his decision, particularly the opportunity to preserve the partnership between Ivan Perisic and Filip Kostic. “There were several advantages to setting it up this way. For instance, it allowed the pairing of Ivan and Filip to remain intact. I also felt Ivan had an aerial advantage over Read,” he added. Van Bommel had two opportunities to score but sent both efforts over the crossbar. Despite his failure to convert, Bosz felt the chances themselves were encouraging. “As for Ruben, he had two chances, though he sent both shots over the bar. Still, the opportunities were there, and that's always something to hold onto.” The PSV manager felt his side are moving in the right direction [IMAGO/ANP] PSV Manager Believes His Side Deserved More Bosz faced criticism following PSV's defeat to ADO Den Haag, which marked their third loss in four matches. However, the victory in Porto and the performance against Feyenoord have given him reason to believe his team are moving in the right direction. The PSV manager felt his side carried their improved form into Sunday's contest, even though they could not turn their dominance into three points. “I think the conclusion is that I was proven right following last week,” Bosz remarked, as relayed by Rik Elfrink of Eindhovens Dagblad . “After that, we played very well in Porto and won. We carried that form into this match, though without the desired result.” He added that PSV had done enough to win the contest. “I believe we were the better side against Feyenoord, and if anyone deserved to win the match, it was us.” The PSV manager was critical of the defending that allowed Hadj-Moussa to equalise [IMAGO/Orange Pictures] Bosz Identifies Defensive Error Behind Hadj-Moussa's Goal While acknowledging Feyenoord's individual quality, Bosz was critical of the defending that allowed Hadj-Moussa to equalise. The winger cut inside from the right and found the far corner with an excellent finish, exposing space around PSV's defensive line. Bosz believed the situation could have been handled better, pointing to a loss of possession from Lutsharel Geertruida and Mauro Júnior's positioning. “Lutsharel lost possession, which was unnecessary. Furthermore, Mauro was just a step too far away, leaving space for a shot. Filip did a good job of shielding the outside. If Mauro had been just one step closer, he could have blocked the shot,” he explained. Despite the setback, Bosz insisted that the title race remained open, with plenty of time for PSV to recover the four-point deficit. “There is plenty of time to make up those four points, and ultimately, it all comes down to which side proves to be the most stable team,” he said, acknowledging that Feyenoord currently hold that advantage. Bosz also explained that his decision to replace Kodai Sano was driven by the desire to find a winner, with Shuryjano Cornecion brought on in the hope of offering more attacking threat. For PSV, the draw was a missed opportunity. However, Bosz believes the performances against Porto and Feyenoord provide a platform from which his side can rebuild momentum and remain in contention for the Eredivisie title.

item.title: Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja reveals secret battle with rheumatoid arthritis
item.description: The former Australia batter Usman Khawaja has revealed that he fought a secret battle with rheumatoid arthritis throughout his international career. Khawaja concluded his time in an Australia shirt at the end of the Ashes in January having featured in 88 Tests and made 18 international hundreds. The left-hander’s success came despite a chronic auto-immune condition first diagnosed when he was 22, though only a select number of medical staff and administrators were made aware – with Khawaja keeping it secret from his teammates and friends. “It was debilitating. I took an injection last night,” Khawaja said in Brisbane as he prepares to release his autobiography. “It was part of the reason that I did my back at the end of my career , but I couldn’t tell anyone. “I never got injured before I had my arthritic illness, but after that I got injured quite a lot and had to find a way to get my body in the right spot. Even my best friend from high school, Ardil, didn’t know until one year ago. “I didn’t want anyone to use it against me. I felt like I already had all these stereotypes I was trying to beat in Australian cricket, and I didn’t want to use that as an excuse.” Khawaja’s autobiography, Sabr , will be released on 10 November and chronicle his journey as the first Muslim cricketer to play internationally for Australia. The 39-year-old, who will play for the Brisbane Heat in the upcoming edition of the Big Bash, did not engage a ghostwriter for his book, believing that only he could pen it in the right way. “I didn’t think anyone could encapsulate my story like I could because no one has been through the same journey in Australian cricket like I have,” Khawaja explained. “The immigrant, brown, Pakistani Muslim kid coming from overseas to play our national game is something I didn’t feel comfortable someone else writing about.” Khawaja has met with Australia captain Pat Cummins ahead of the release, with the “Sandpaper-gate” saga in South Africa in 2018 covered within the book.

item.title: Today's 5️⃣ stories: 🥐 Ballon d'Or day, a lesson from Mourinho
item.description: Today's 5️⃣ stories: 🥐 Ballon d'Or day, a lesson from Mourinho What a Monday! We're still catching our breath after El Clásico and a weekend packed with football, with the Ballon d'Or ceremony just around the corner. Before this spectacular day gets underway, let's run through the five stories you can't miss. José Mourinho's night 📸 Alex Caparros - 2026 Getty Images Real Madrid won El Clásico at the Camp Nou, and José Mourinho's game plan proved a masterstroke. After a few months in which Barcelona had shown their superiority and Real Madrid had spread pessimism, the Portuguese coach pocketed another epic victory. Kylian Mbappé's goals, Cucurella's outstanding display and Jude Bellingham's performance led Los Blancos to victory and blew the title race wide open, with Atlético Madrid joining the fight. Ballon d'Or day 📸 FRANCK FIFE - AFP or licensors Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal and Rodri are the leading favourites to win the Ballon d'Or. The ceremony in Paris gets underway today at 9pm, and it will be a very happy day for one of these four. You can follow it on OneFootball with our live coverage. Carrick all but out at Manchester United 📸 DARREN STAPLES - AFP or licensors Manchester United lost again. This time, it was a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford. After Lisandro Martínez criticised the board following the defeat at the Metropolitano, Bruno Fernandes spoke out after the embarrassment in Como, and United lost to Bournemouth, Carrick's fate appears to be sealed. Reports in England suggest he is expected to be sacked soon. Bayern reaffirm their place as joint leaders 📸 THOMAS KIENZLE - AFP or licensors Bayern Munich beat Freiburg 3-1 to move joint top of the Bundesliga. With Kompany dealing with health issues and Kimmich mourning the death of a family member, the Bavarians managed to beat third-placed Freiburg and keep pace with Borussia Dortmund. Inter, Juventus and Milan get the job done 📸 Marco Luzzani - 2026 Getty Images Little has changed in the Italian standings after this weekend. Inter, Lazio, Milan, Como and Juventus all got the job done. Meanwhile, Roma were the only side near the top to drop points, drawing 3-3 with Napoli. The Nerazzurri came from behind to beat Fiorentina in stoppage time and stay top, while Milan won in Udine on Sunday and Juventus did the same in Lecce. item.title: Cristian Chivu refuses to take credit for a 'devastating' Marcus Thuram after Inter's miraculous 98th-minute comeback against Fiorentina
item.description: FC Internazionale v ACF Fiorentina - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Cristian Chivu was in awe of his star striker Marcus Thuram after a breathless 2-1 victory over Fiorentina sent Inter to the top of Serie A. The Nerazzurri boss is refusing to take the spotlight for Thuram's blistering evolution, jokingly pointing the finger at Zinedine Zidane after the French forward orchestrated a stunning stoppage-time comeback against Fiorentina. Catalyst Thuram sparks sensational late fightback Thuram proved to be the catalyst for the turnaround, scoring the equalising goal before earning the penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the 98th minute. Thuram stepped up as the focal point of the attack in the absence of Lautaro Martinez due to injury. Chivu was quick to praise the striker's relentless work rate and physical dominance during the final stages of the match. The Inter boss even joked about the influences on Thuram's recent form, including his time with the French national team legend Zinedine Zidane. "I don't know if it's my merit or Zidane's. Without Lautaro, he took on the responsibility. I was with him for three weeks and he had a rest, which is why I said I don't know if it's my merit or Zidane's. He would even sprint in the 90th minute, entering the penalty area with devastating ferocity," Chivu said, as quoted by Sky Sport Italia . Zidane's snub lights Thuram's fire Following Didier Deschamps' departure from the French national team, Thuram was left out of Zidane's inaugural squad as the new manager initiated a broad tactical overhaul. Rather than allowing the international snub to hinder his momentum, the forward channeled the setback into sharp on-pitch focus, using the exclusion as extra motivation to elevate his club performances. "Today and in Bologna, when he attacks you with that speed, there's a risk that something will happen. We're happy; we gave him a day off tomorrow even though the team will train. He and the others will be rested. Why didn't he take the penalty? We have great penalty takers. He enjoys watching the others and is an added value for us. Not being called up gave him extra motivation," Chivu noted. Tactical changes pay dividends Chivu also addressed the decision-making process behind the late penalty, which saw Zielinski step up instead of the man who won the foul. The coach emphasised that individual accolades matter less than the collective effort within the dressing room. "We have great penalty takers. He enjoys watching the others and he is an added value for us. Not being called up gave him extra motivation," Chivu stated. The manager also discussed his tactical substitutions, which included bringing on young talent Matteo Lavelli to bolster the attack. item.content:encoded: FC Internazionale v ACF Fiorentina - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Cristian Chivu was in awe of his star striker Marcus Thuram after a breathless 2-1 victory over Fiorentina sent Inter to the top of Serie A. The Nerazzurri boss is refusing to take the spotlight for Thuram's blistering evolution, jokingly pointing the finger at Zinedine Zidane after the French forward orchestrated a stunning stoppage-time comeback against Fiorentina. Catalyst Thuram sparks sensational late fightback Thuram proved to be the catalyst for the turnaround, scoring the equalising goal before earning the penalty that Piotr Zielinski converted in the 98th minute. Thuram stepped up as the focal point of the attack in the absence of Lautaro Martinez due to injury. Chivu was quick to praise the striker's relentless work rate and physical dominance during the final stages of the match. The Inter boss even joked about the influences on Thuram's recent form, including his time with the French national team legend Zinedine Zidane. "I don't know if it's my merit or Zidane's. Without Lautaro, he took on the responsibility. I was with him for three weeks and he had a rest, which is why I said I don't know if it's my merit or Zidane's. He would even sprint in the 90th minute, entering the penalty area with devastating ferocity," Chivu said, as quoted by Sky Sport Italia . Zidane's snub lights Thuram's fire Following Didier Deschamps' departure from the French national team, Thuram was left out of Zidane's inaugural squad as the new manager initiated a broad tactical overhaul. Rather than allowing the international snub to hinder his momentum, the forward channeled the setback into sharp on-pitch focus, using the exclusion as extra motivation to elevate his club performances. "Today and in Bologna, when he attacks you with that speed, there's a risk that something will happen. We're happy; we gave him a day off tomorrow even though the team will train. He and the others will be rested. Why didn't he take the penalty? We have great penalty takers. He enjoys watching the others and is an added value for us. Not being called up gave him extra motivation," Chivu noted. Tactical changes pay dividends Chivu also addressed the decision-making process behind the late penalty, which saw Zielinski step up instead of the man who won the foul. The coach emphasised that individual accolades matter less than the collective effort within the dressing room. "We have great penalty takers. He enjoys watching the others and he is an added value for us. Not being called up gave him extra motivation," Chivu stated. The manager also discussed his tactical substitutions, which included bringing on young talent Matteo Lavelli to bolster the attack. He insisted that age is not a factor when he selects his lineup, preferring to focus on the specific needs of the game and the energy levels of his squad. "I chose to add a striker to fill the area since we weren't able to with the mezzali . I don't look at the identity card of either [Henrikh] Mkhitaryan or Lavelli. Sometimes it's not easy to get into the team and not everything goes as you'd like: they have to be ready," he added. Belief until the final whistle The victory keeps Inter firmly in the hunt at the top of the Serie A table, level with Lazio. Chivu acknowledged that while his players were exhausted due to the heavy fixture schedule, their fighting spirit carried them through. He noted that although falling behind early in games is not ideal, the team must continue to embrace the challenge and avoid creating a "case" out of their habit for staging late comebacks. "Even if energy was low, they put their hearts into it against an organised team. We showed grit, which isn't always visible because we play every three days. Sometimes going behind can create doubts; we must not let ourselves get down or become satisfied, and we must always have the same desire to win. It will happen that we go ahead and then lose, but we shouldn't make a big deal of it, just as we don't now," the manager concluded.

item.title: Gary Neville attacks ‘nothing’ Man United players for giving up on Michael Carrick
item.description: Gary Neville launched an attack on Manchester United ’s players and accused them of giving up on Michael Carrick , who is under mounting pressure following the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday. The manager dropped captain Bruno Fernandes after his criticism of Carrick’s tactics following the 4-1 defeat to Como in midweek while Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the United hierarchy following the loss at Atletico Madrid earlier this month. United are now without a win in eight games and Neville, a former team-mate of Carrick’s under Sir Alex Ferguson, was critical of the current squad’s professionalism and standards following a remarkable unravelling under Carrick this season. Neville defended Carrick and called him a man of ‘integrity’ (Reuters) Neville accused United’s players of walking around like “kings” even though “they are nothing” and said the club’s problems run far deeper than Carrick. “Michael Carrick is a brilliant man,” Neville on Sky Sports . “He's a man of integrity, of credibility, of decency, of professionalism, of high-quality football and consistency and reliability. Everything the group of players in that dressing room aren’t. “And he's going to suffer for it because he's not been able to deliver. It's been too much for him in these last few months. He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. “I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes. “If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific. "There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should. “Why? Because it's gone to their heads. But they still walk around like King William. They are nothing, some of those players.” Bruno Fernandes stayed on the bench against Bournemouth (PA Wire) Carrick spoke for almost six minutes at the start of his pre-match press conference on Friday, imploring the importance of “sacrifice”, “humility” and “hard work” in an impassioned speech which highlighted the “values” of the club and “respecting” the responsibility of representing United. But while Carrick was applauded off the pitch by United’s fans, there were boos for the players and Neville said they produced a “nothing of a performance”. “Nothing against Tottenham here, nothing against Como, nothing against Atletico Madrid. A little bit against Leeds, it was a bit of a fight, but nothing against Fulham. That was a waste of time,” he said. “So, this is a pattern of nothings, of players switching off and downing tools.”

item.title: ‘Assassin Still In There’ — Kurt Warner Fires Back After Fan Claims He’s Gone Soft Following Steelers-Saints Apology
item.description: Nov 11, 2022; Munich, Germany; Kurt Warner attends Tampa Bay Buccaneers practice at the FC Bayern Campus. © Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Kurt Warner made a mistake in the booth on Sunday that he couldn’t take back, and the Hall of Famer didn’t run from it. During NFL Network’s broadcast of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 7 at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, France, Warner repeatedly called Steelers RB Jaylen Warren “Tyler,” mixing him up with Indianapolis Colts TE Tyler Warren. Warner apologized on X that afternoon, writing, “I own it.” Late Sunday night, a little more than eight hours later, he posted again, this time with a message about accountability. By then, the mix-up had made the rounds online. Kurt Warner Reflects on Steelers-Saints Broadcasting Mistake Warner first issued an apology after admitting he made a mistake on the broadcast. After that apology, one fan puzzlingly accused Warner of going soft, saying that he wanted the 2-time MVP “assassin” back, not a man who apologizes for his mistakes. Warner’s follow-up was short and pointed: “Relax… assassin still in there, and it was the guy that always kept himself accountable to chase greatness!!!” Then came the line the post turned on: “If you’re not chasing greatness and admitting mistakes, you never become the assassin; you get killed along the way!” One slip came in the middle of a compliment. Warner, who called the game alongside Dave Pasch and Jason Kelce, was praising Jaylen Warren’s work as a receiver when he said, “Not when you’ve got Tyler Warren on the field… Nobody better in the league at the running back spot of yards-after-catch than Tyler Warren.” His booth partners eventually corrected him. On the field, Jaylen Warren ran 18 times for 101 yards and caught three passes for 36 more. Tyler Warren, meanwhile, spent the day with the Colts in Minneapolis, where they played the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium. It was National Tight Ends Day, of all Sundays. The two Warrens had shared a field two weeks earlier, when the Steelers beat the Colts 34-22 in Pittsburgh on Oct. 11. Meanwhile, Warner addressed it the same day. The game kicked off at 9:30 a.m. ET, and his apology went up shortly after 3 p.m. ET, putting the right name front and center and pointing to where the wrong one came from: “Yes, I called JAYLEN Warren ‘Tyler’ today after calling Colts game & referencing him in today’s game.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer He followed with a broadcaster’s confession: “My bad, so sorry… It stinks as an announcer when you do that, and unfortunately it won’t be my last time because sometimes you just react and misspeak!” And he made sure the running back got his due: “JAYLEN was awesome today, so hopefully I gave him enough love at other times!!” Jaylen Warren’s carries made up most of Pittsburgh’s 148 rushing yards in a game decided by six points, and his 29-yard run was the longest of the game for either team. item.title: Chiefs Coach Andy Reid Assigns Blame After Brutal Seahawks Loss
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Andy Reid of the Kansas City Chiefs prepares to take the field prior to the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) Getty Kansas City Chiefs coach Andy Reid is taking the blame for his team’s dismal loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs looked sluggish on offense and struggled to contain the Seahawks on defense, falling 20-3 for their first loss of the season. Reid admitted after the game that he should have done a better job of getting his team ready for the challenge of playing the reigning Super Bowl champions in a prime-time matchup. Andy Reid Speaks Out After Brutal Loss Speaking to reporters after the loss, Reid said the Seahawks dominated the game and said it was on him to have the Chiefs better prepared. “Listen, all three phases we struggled, so we’ve got to do better, and that’s my responsibility,” Andy Reid said after the game. “So I take full responsibility for this. We’ve got to play better as a team.” The Chiefs came into the game with one of the league’s top offenses, balancing a rushing game built behind league-leading Kenneth Walker III with a passing game led by the resilient Patrick Mahomes in his return from a season-ending injury. But the Seahawks stymied both phases, holding the Chiefs to 213 total yards on offense while holding them without a touchdown. ESPN Insights noted after the game that it was the first time in Mahomes’ career that his team was held without a single drive reaching the red zone. It was also the lowest scoring output of Mahomes’ career, with the Chiefs scoring just 3 points and missing two field goals. Reid said after the game that kicker Harrison Butker was “off,” but didn’t specify exactly what he meant. Reid said the veteran kicker would work this week to get back on track. “Listen, he’s been one of the most consistent kickers in football,” Reid said, via SI.com . “He’s off a bit. So, we’ve got to fix that.” Chiefs Struggled to Get Off the Field on Defense ESPN’s Nate Taylor noted that the Chiefs shared the misery on both sides of the ball. He noted that midway through the third quarter, the Seahawks had doubled the possession time of the Chiefs and ran more than twice as many plays. “The reason for such a disparity was that the Chiefs’ defense couldn’t get off the field, as the unit allowed the Seahawks to convert on 11 of 16 third downs,” Taylor wrote. “Even when longtime defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo blitzed, Darnold was able to find the easy answer. Most often, that answer was to throw the ball to Smith-Njigba, who shredded the Chiefs’ secondary repeatedly.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Chiefs Coach Andy Reid Assigns Blame After Brutal Seahawks Loss appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: NFL Legend Launches 21-Word Criticism of Xavier Worthy as Chiefs Offense Fails to Show Up in SNF Loss to Seahawks
item.description: NFL Legend Launches 21-Word Criticism of Xavier Worthy as Chiefs Offense Fails to Show Up in SNF Loss to Seahawks The Kansas City Chiefs’ 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks exposed familiar problems with their passing game, and Shannon Sharpe believes Xavier Worthy is part of the problem. With Rashee Rice sidelined by injury, Worthy had an opportunity to step up as Patrick Mahomes’ primary wide receiver. Instead, he managed just 11 receiving yards as Seattle handed Kansas City its first loss of the season. Shannon Sharpe Questions Xavier Worthy’s Route-Running Technique Worthy delivered a solid performance in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, recording seven receptions on seven targets for 73 yards. However, his production took a sharp dip against the Seahawks, as he struggled to create separation from defenders and dropped a pass in a crucial second-half situation. Seattle’s defense effectively neutralized Worthy’s impact, and he finished Sunday’s loss with just three receptions on six targets for 11 yards. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Following Worthy’s disappointing outing, Sharpe posted to criticize the wideout’s approach to route-running. “Worthy just takes off running no move or anything. Speed isn’t any good IF* you don’t know how 2 use it,” Sharpe tweeted a 21-word reaction. Sharpe’s criticism came after Kansas City’s offense struggled to find any rhythm against Seattle. The Seahawks limited the Chiefs to 213 total yards and 11 first downs while holding them to just three conversions on 11 third-down attempts. Kansas City also failed to reach the red zone throughout the game, with its deepest advance coming to Seattle’s 27-yard line. The offensive struggles prompted Sharpe to express his frustration during a later appearance on the “Nightcap” podcast, where he questioned the quality of the Chiefs’ receiving corps after watching their performance against the Seahawks. Sharpe also said that he was “very disappointed” in Worthy, who finished second on Kansas City with six targets, behind Travis Kelce’s eight, but he ranked sixth on the team in receiving yards in the Seahawks game. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “If you watch him play, he’s fast for no reason,” Sharpe said . “If you look at him with him in the slot, that is a safety or a linebacker guarding you, and he’s running step for step guy. Why? Because all you did was badly. “You didn’t give him a move. You didn’t give a nod. You didn’t stutter. You didn’t do anything.” Worthy’s struggles have drawn attention because of his exceptional speed, which made him one of the most elite prospects in the 2024 NFL Draft. At the 2024 NFL Scouting Combine, Worthy ran the 40-yard dash in 4.21 seconds, setting a new combine record at the time. item.title: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley gives heartfelt reaction to first NFL win after beating Jets
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley gives heartfelt reaction to first NFL win after beating Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley celebrated an emotional milestone after his team defeated the New York Jets. 28-25 on Sunday. The victory ended Miami’s winless start and followed a game in which the Dolphins finally took their first lead of the season. Hafley earned his first victory as an NFL head coach at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, his home state. “I wanted them to feel this,” Hafley said in a postgame interview shared by The List Dolphins Podcast. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The coach credited his players with staying committed despite five straight losses to open the campaign. “All the hard work, all the things we’ve been asking them to do since OTA’s,” Hafley explained. “That’s one we’ll all remember as we build this thing.” Hafley also described the celebrations inside Miami’s locker room, where players showered him with water following the victory. “I grabbed every guy when I went in, I had so much water dumped on me,” he said. Quarterback Malik Willis helped deliver the milestone, throwing for 208 yards and two touchdowns. He also rushed for another score as Miami survived New York’s late comeback attempt. Rookie receiver Caleb Douglas caught both touchdown passes, including a crucial 63-yard strike in the fourth quarter. The victory also ended the uncertainty surrounding Miami’s early-season struggles. Despite the celebrations, Hafley emphasized that one victory would not change his approach. “Regardless of anything, the process is always going to be the most important thing to me,” he said. Miami now turns its attention to next Sunday’s divisional matchup against the New England Patriots. Related: It took until Week 7 for Dolphins to actually lead in a game

item.title: Rams’ Week 7 win over Raiders was major statement that LA is still a Super Bowl contender
item.description: Rams’ Week 7 win over Raiders was major statement that LA is still a Super Bowl contender appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams badly needed a statement win . Well, they delivered one in emphatic fashion. After a frustrating stretch of close defeats, Sean McVay ’s team dismantled the Las Vegas Raiders, 35-21, on Sunday. Matthew Stafford looked sharp, the running game imposed its will, and the offense found creative ways to produce without Davante Adams. The defense also controlled Las Vegas on the ground. At 3-4, Los Angeles still has work to do. However, this performance offered a timely reminder that its championship aspirations should not be dismissed. Changed the narrative Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Rams entered Week 7 coming off consecutive one-score losses to Buffalo and Arizona. They were painfully searching for answers. Los Angeles found them in Las Vegas, racing to a 28-6 halftime lead behind four consecutive touchdown drives. Stafford completed 23 of 29 passes for 195 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception. He also became the franchise’s all-time leader in passing touchdowns with 155. Davis Allen caught two scoring passes. Puka Nacua added another . Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 192 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Las Vegas mounted a fourth-quarter push, but Corum’s late touchdown restored breathing room and helped Los Angeles close out a convincing road victory. Tactical identity The most encouraging takeaway was how McVay adapted without Adams. His absence has created a significant hole in the receiving corps, particularly on the boundary. Against Las Vegas, the Rams demonstrated that their offense can still function at a high level by spreading the workload and leaning into favorable matchups. An offense like this, whcih can hurt opponents through multiple personnel groupings and a productive ground game, is much harder to contain. The Rams have not solved every issue, of course. The defense was not flawless. Cousins threw for 295 yards. The Raiders briefly made the score uncomfortable with two fourth-quarter touchdowns. Stafford’s interception also handed Las Vegas a short field. Those lapses are worth addressing before tougher opponents arrive. Even so, the Rams showed they can establish control when their offense creates a favorable game script. Their ability to stop the run and force opponents into more obvious passing situations gives the defense a foundation to build on. Potential second-half surge The Rams should not mistake one victory for a complete turnaround. At 3-4, they remain below .500, and the NFC race leaves little room for another extended losing streak. Adams’ return timeline also remains uncertain. As such, Los Angeles must continue finding production from its available personnel. Still, the immediate schedule offers opportunities to build momentum. The Rams host the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8 before traveling to face Washington and Arizona. A strong run through that stretch could move them back toward the playoff picture before their late-season push. The front office must also remain realistic about injuries. If the Rams improve their late-game execution and build on Sunday’s performance, their season can still develop into something meaningful. The Super Bowl conversation should remain open. Los Angeles has not proved it belongs among the NFC’s elite just yet. However, it has made one thing clear: writing off the Rams after a difficult start would be premature. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
item.description: At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher. item.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
item.description: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.” Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

item.description: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone Braga and Miller give Hearts 2-0 win at Motherwell Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road. After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break. item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: European football: Lazio beat Parma to top Serie A; Dortmund lead Bundesliga
item.description: Lazio win 2-1 while Roma draw 3-3 with Napoli Beier gives Dortmund win over Eintracht Frankfurt Lazio climbed to the top of Serie A with a 2-1 home win ⁠over Parma ⁠as Roma ​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating clash in Naples. Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. The visitors scored a ‌late consolation through Simone Lontani. Continue reading...

item.title: Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems go | Barney Ronay
item.description: Home side broke the game open with some unique corner routines, but a goalkeeping error ruined the plan There was an odd interlude at Stamford Bridge with 76 minutes gone and the score still 0-0, one of those moments where suddenly your brain seems to be on inside out, like trying to walk the wrong way down an escalator. Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Continue reading...

item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Nicolas Jackson double sees Aston Villa end Manchester City’s perfect start
item.description: Manchester City added a loss in the Premier League to one to the Premier League, as their perfect record this season vanished without an independent commission in sight. Two of the most in-form strikers in England did battle and it was Nicolas Jackson’s double that meant his side came out on top against Erling Haaland. City are certainly fallible, losing for the fourth time in a row here, and it was a reminder that life will not always be as simple as their first seven games. Mistakes cost City as Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma were punished by Jackson, who will have taken great pleasure in ending the winning run of his former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...
